children.text: pañcapañcasaṃkhyāvacchinnāḥ samudāyāḥ pañcakā lābhādayas teṣāṃ nyūnādhikavyavacchedena aṣṭa iti saṃkhyām āha ||
children.translated_text: The aggregates delimited by the number five are pentads, beginning with gains; by distinguishing what is deficient and what is additional among them, he states the number eight.

children.text: tuśabdaḥ saṃkṣepavistāraparijñānayoḥ tulyaphalatvam avadhārayati śiṣyajijñāsānurodhena bhāṣyārambho 'py arthavān iti ||
children.translated_text: The word “but” determines that concise and expanded understanding have the same result, and that the beginning of the commentary too is meaningful in accordance with the student’s desire to know.

children.text: vijñeyā viśeṣeṇa jñātavyāḥ punaḥ punar abhyāsena dṛḍhīkartavyā yena sarvadā śāstrārthe cittasthe kṛte sati granthavismaraṇe 'pi brahmodyadoṣo na bhavet ||
children.translated_text: They are to be known, that is, to be understood distinctly, and made firm again and again by practice, so that when the meaning of the śāstra has always been placed in the mind, even if the text is forgotten, there will be no fault in doctrinal disputation.

children.text: anuṣṭhānāśaktasyānyathā hi surāpānasamaṃ pātakaṃ syād iti ||
children.translated_text: Otherwise, for one incapable of performance, there would be a sin equal to drinking liquor.
The word “group” denotes a collection.

children.text: caśabdaḥ samuccayena kevalam aṣṭa pañcakā vijñeyā gaṇaś caikas trikātmako vijñeya iti ||
children.translated_text: The word “and” means that, by way of collection, only the eight pentads are to be known, and also one group whose nature is triadic is to be known.
The word “one” is for removing the doubt that the number eight just mentioned applies here too.
An aggregate delimited by the number three is a triad.

children.text: sa eva ātmā svabhāvo yasya bhaikṣādivṛttigaṇasya sa tathoktaḥ vṛttyantaraniṣedhārtham ||
children.translated_text: That very self, that is, the nature, belongs to the group of modes of livelihood beginning with begging; it is so called in order to exclude other modes of livelihood.
Thus these nine groups are specified as objects to be known.

children.text: yas tān samyag avadhārayati so 'vaśyaṃ duḥkhāntaṃ yāsyaty anyeṣāṃ cānugrahakaraṇasamartho bhavatīti ||
children.translated_text: He who ascertains them correctly will necessarily go to the end of suffering, and becomes capable of doing favor to others as well.
But from where is this determined?

children.text: niścīyate yasmāt sarvair eva paramayogibhiḥ vettā navagaṇasyāsya saṃskartā gurur ucyate ||
children.translated_text: It is determined because all supreme yogins say: “The knower of this ninefold group, the consecrator, is called guru.”
The root vid means “to know.”

children.text: tasya vediteti prāpte chandobhaṅgaparihārārthaṃ chāndasaḥ prayogo vettā iti kṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When “his knower” would be expected, the Vedic-style usage “knower” was made in order to avoid breaking the meter.
Or else, in the sense of deliberation, the form means “one who considers it.”
A knower is one who examines.

children.text: navagaṇānām iti bahuvacane prāpte chandobhaṅgaparihārārthaṃ tatparijñānasya bhinnaphalatvajñāpanārthaṃ vā navagaṇasya ity uktam ||
children.translated_text: When the plural “of the nine groups” would be expected, “of the ninefold group” was said either to avoid breaking the meter or to indicate that the knowledge of them has a distinct result.

children.text: nandimahākālādiṣv api gaṇaśabdo dṛṣṭaḥ tadāśaṅkānirākaraṇārtham asyety uktam ||
children.translated_text: The word “group” is also seen in such expressions as the attendants of <s>Nandin</s> and <s>Mahākāla</s>; to remove that possible doubt, the word “this” is used.
“This” means the group beginning with gains that was specified immediately before.

children.text: suparīkṣitaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ dīkṣāviśeṣeṇa pañcārthajñānaviśeṣeṇa ca śiṣyaṃ saṃskurvan saṃskartā ity ucyate ||
children.translated_text: When he consecrates a well-tested brāhmaṇa as a disciple by a particular initiation and by a particular knowledge of the five topics, he is called the consecrator.

children.text: sa ca tajjñair mukhyata eva gurur ucyate ||
children.translated_text: And he is called guru in the primary sense by those who know that matter.

children.text: gurur ācāryaḥ śraddhāvatām āśramiṇāṃ darśanasambhāṣaṇādibhir api pāpaghnaḥ puṇyātiśayakārī cety arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Guru means teacher; for householders and ascetics who have faith, even by seeing and conversing with him and the like, he destroys sin and produces an abundance of merit.
Alternatively, the connection of the verse is shown in another way.

children.text: dvividhaḥ khalv atra brāhmaṇo 'pavargagantā śrūyate sādhaka ācāryaś ceti ||
children.translated_text: For here two kinds of brāhmaṇa are heard of as going to liberation: the practitioner and the teacher.

children.text: tatreha darśane yaḥ sādhakaḥ sann apavargaṃ gantum icchati ||
children.translated_text: Among them, in this system, the practitioner is the one who, being a practitioner, wishes to go to liberation.

children.text: śāstraṃ śrutvācāryopadeśamātrād vā vidhyādisvarūpaṃ jñātvā vidhiyogānuṣṭhānam atyantābhiyogena kartavyam ||
children.translated_text: Having heard the śāstra, or merely from the teacher’s instruction, and having known the nature of injunction and the rest, he must perform the practice of injunction-yoga with utmost application.

children.text: yas tv ācāryaḥ sann apavargam gantum icchati tena kiṃ kartavyam iti āha ||
children.translated_text: But what must one who is a teacher and wishes to go to liberation do? In answer to this he says:

children.text: pañcakās tv aṣṭa vijñeyā gaṇaś caikas trikātmakaḥ iti ||
children.translated_text: “Eight pentads are to be known, and one group whose nature is triadic.”

children.text: tuśabdaḥ samastasūtrasūtrāvayavānām upodghātādiniścayadvāreṇa navagaṇā vijñeyās tān vijñāya śiṣyāṇāṃ saṃśayād yajñānaṃ nirvartayatā saṃskāraḥ kartavya ity evaṃbhūtaṃ viśeṣaṃ sūcayati ||
children.translated_text: The word “but” indicates this specific point: through determining the introduction and so on of all the sūtras and parts of sūtras, the nine groups are to be known; having known them, one should perform consecration while bringing about knowledge in the disciples from their doubts.
The remaining meaning of the components is as before.
But how is this understood?

children.text: duḥkhanimittam ācāryatvam ātmana icchatā navagaṇā viśeṣato jñātavyā iti gamyate ||
children.translated_text: It is understood that the nine groups are to be known particularly by one who desires teacherhood, which is the cause of the end of suffering, for himself.
Because:

children.text: evaṃ cānuṣṭhānābhiniveśāsamartho 'pi yadi śraddhānvito bhūtveṣad api samayamātraṃ pālayan jñānābhyāsaṃ na muñcati tadāpavargagantā bhavaty ācārya iti cocyate ||
children.translated_text: And thus, even if he is incapable of devotion to practice, if, being endowed with faith, he protects even a little of the prescribed observance for merely some time and does not abandon the cultivation of knowledge, he becomes one who goes to liberation and is called a teacher.

children.text: yas tv āgamārthajñānamātreṇa tuṣṭaḥ san śraddhādivirahitaḥ śraddhādimātrayukto vā lābhādijñānavikalaḥ sa khalv ācāryābhāsa eva nāpavargaganteti ||
children.translated_text: But one who is satisfied with mere knowledge of the meaning of the tradition, devoid of faith and the rest, or possessed only of faith and the rest but lacking knowledge of gains and the other categories, is indeed only a semblance of a teacher and does not go to liberation.
Then the nature of the groups must be stated.

children.text: ke 'ṣṭa pañcakāḥ kaś ca trikātmako gaṇaḥ ity ata āha ||
children.translated_text: Which are the eight pentads, and what is the group whose nature is triadic? Therefore he says:

children.text: vidhīyamānam upāyaphalaṃ lābhaḥ athavā jñānatapodevanityatvasthitisiddhibhedabhinnā lābhāḥ athavānabhivyaktapūrvā bhāvāḥ sādhakātmani vyajyamānā lābhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Gain is the means and result being enjoined; or the gains are divided into knowledge, austerity, divinity, eternality, stability, and perfection; or gains are states not previously manifest that become manifest in the self of the practitioner.

children.text: yeṣām ātmāśritānāṃ bhāvānāṃ kṣapaṇārthaṃ sādhakaḥ prayatate te malāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those states, residing in the self, for the destruction of which the practitioner strives, are impurities.
Or the impurities are divided into false knowledge, non-dharma, attachment, falling away, and animality.
The means are the most effective aids of the practitioner and the causes of purification and increase.
Or the means are divided into residence, conduct, recitation, meditation, constant recollection, and favor.

children.text: caśabdaḥ pādapūraṇe lābhādīnāṃ vā parasparāsaṃkīrṇalakṣaṇasūtraka iti ||
children.translated_text: The word “and” is for filling out the metrical quarter, or else it is a sūtra marking the mutually unmixed definitions of gains and the others.

children.text: deśāś cāvasthāś ca viśuddhayaś ceti dvaṃdvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: “Places, states, and purifications” is a compound of paired terms.

children.text: yadāśrayasāmarthyena sādhakaḥ śuddhivṛddhī prāpnoti te deśā gurujanaguhāśmaśānarudralakṣaṇā iti vakṣyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those by whose supporting power the practitioner attains purification and increase are places; we shall say that they are characterized as the teacher, people, a cave, a cremation ground, and <s>Rudra</s>.

children.text: ālābhaprāpter ekamaryādayāvasthitayaḥ sādhakasya avasthās tā vyaktādiviśeṣeṇa viśiṣṭā vakṣyante ||
children.translated_text: Since gain has not yet been obtained, the states of the practitioner, established within a single limit, will be explained as qualified by distinctions such as manifestation and the like.
Purifications are the complete removals of false knowledge and the other impurities.
The expression is a paired compound: consecrating factors and powers.

The consecrating factors are the causes of consecration, named substance, time, action, image, and guru; they are factors belonging to the self of the practitioner and causes for undertaking the means.
The powers are characterized as devotion to the guru, clarity of understanding, favor, conquest of the pair of opposites, <s>dharma</s>, and vigilance.
The phrase “eight pentads” is the summing up.

children.text: tisro vṛttaya iti prāpte trīṇi vṛttaya iti chāndasaḥ prayogaḥ kṛtaḥ pañcamalaghūkaraṇārtham ||
children.translated_text: Although “three modes of livelihood” would be expected, the Vedic-style usage “three livelihoods” was made in order to avoid making the fifth syllable light.
Livelihoods are means of acquiring food that do not conflict with the āgama; they are called begging, abandoned food, and what is obtained as it comes.

children.text: tatra prathamāvasthasya tāvad bhaikṣam eva vṛttis tasyāḥ ko vidhir ity ucyate ||
children.translated_text: Among these, for one in the first state, begging alone is the livelihood. What is the rule for it? This is now stated.

children.text: jñātvā bhikṣākālaṃ śucir bhūtvā bhasmanā hastau prakṣālya pātraṃ gṛhītvā udakaprakṣālitaṃ saṃskṛtaṃ ca kṛtvā mahādevaṃ praṇamyānujñāṃ prārthayet tadanu gurūn iti ||
children.translated_text: Having known the time for begging, becoming pure, washing the hands with ash, taking the bowl, rinsing it with water and consecrating it, bowing to <s>Mahādeva</s>, he should ask permission, and after that from the gurus.

children.text: tato devagurubhir anujñāto mantrān āvartayan īśvarāsaktacitto vā dṛṣṭipūtena pathābhiśastapatitagṛhāṇi varjayitvā yatra ca bhayanimittaṃ ca kākādi kaluṣanimittaṃ cāmedhyavivastrayuvativiṭadurjanavacanabhikṣukākīrṇatvādy upalabhyate tadgṛhāṇy api varjayann ekam eva grāmādīnām anyatamaṃ paryaṭed yady antarāle eva paryāptir na bhavati upaghāto vā kaścid iti tataḥ svāyatanam āgatyāparādhānurūpaṃ prāyaścittaṃ kṛtvā mantrasaṃskṛtaṃ ca kṛtvā tadbhaikṣaṃ śivāyānugurave ca nivedya maheśvaraṃ hṛdi saṃdhāya saṃyatavāgudaṅmukhaḥ prāṅmukho vā samarasaṃ kṛtvoparyupari vā bhuñjīteti ||
children.translated_text: Then, permitted by the deity and the gurus, reciting mantras, or with his mind attached to <s>Īśvara</s>, he should wander by a path purified by sight, avoiding the houses of the accursed and fallen, and also avoiding houses where a cause of fear is perceived, or an impure sign such as crows and the like, or where there is pollution through something impure, an unclothed young woman, a lecher, bad people’s speech, or a crowd of beggars. He should go around only one among villages and the like. If, on the way, enough is not obtained or some injury occurs, then, returning to his own residence, he should perform expiation according to the offense, consecrate that alms-food with mantras, offer it to <s>Śiva</s> and to the attendant guru, place <s>Maheśvara</s> in his heart, restrain his speech, face north or east, make the food uniform in taste, and eat it from top to bottom.

children.text: pātraṃ pātraśaucaṃ ca sūtrānumataṃ smṛtiprasiddhaṃ pratipattavyam ||
children.translated_text: The bowl and the purification of the bowl are to be understood as approved by sūtra and well known in smṛti.
Thus <s>Yājñavalkya</s> says:
The vessels of an ascetic are made of clay, bamboo, wood, and bottle-gourd.
Their purification is with water, and by rubbing with cow-hair.
<s>Manu</s> also says:

children.text: ataijasāni pātrāṇi tasya syur nirvraṇāni ca
children.translated_text: His vessels should be non-metallic and without cracks.
Their purification is remembered as being with water, like ladles in a sacrifice.

children.text: sāpannaṃ ca salepaṃ ca vibhinnaṃ cāpi yadbhavet
children.translated_text: If a vessel should be defective, coated with residue, or even broken,

children.text: tatra bhuktvā ca pītvā ca yatiścāndrāyaṇaṃ caret ||
children.translated_text: then, after eating and drinking from it, an ascetic should perform a <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s> observance.
So says <s>Yama</s>.

children.text: āgamāvirodhigrahaṇād ekānnasya vidyākhyāpanānuśāsanalokayātrādibhir nimittair arjitabhaikṣasya pratiṣedho draṣṭavya ityeṣā prātipadāvasthasya vidhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because the text says “not conflicting with the āgama,” a prohibition is to be understood against alms-food obtained from a single patron or acquired through causes such as teaching knowledge, instruction, or ordinary worldly activity. This is the rule for one in the first state.
This is also the rule for one in the third state.
There is only this much difference here.
One in the third state does not perform expiation, offering, recitation of the five brahmans, subsequent bathing, and the like, because he is a supreme yogin.
For one in the second state, abandoned food alone is the livelihood.

children.text: devādyuddeśena parityaktamannapānaṃ kāruṇyakautūhalābhyāṃ vā yadi kaścid aduṣṭajātir dadyād aśucitvādidoṣarahitaṃ tadutsṛṣṭam ||
children.translated_text: Food and drink set aside for a deity and the like, or if some person of uncorrupted birth gives something out of compassion or curiosity and it is free from faults such as impurity, that is called abandoned food.
And that is to be used without division by māyā.
Since begging has ceased, there is no fixed rule about the bowl.
For one in the fourth state, the livelihood is what is obtained as it comes.

children.text: śmaśānadeśāvasthitenaiva divase divasadvaye traye vā yad annapānaṃ prāpyate tadyathālabdham ucyate ||
children.translated_text: Food and drink that are obtained while one remains in the cremation-ground region for a day, two days, or three days is called what is obtained as it comes.
But for one in the fifth state, because there is no body, livelihood is simply impossible.

children.text: granthakramasya aprādhānyam arthajñānasyaiva prādhānyaṃ manyamāno'krameṇaiva nirdeśaṃ karoti gurubhaktiḥ ityādinā ||
children.translated_text: Considering the order of the text to be secondary and knowledge of the meaning alone to be primary, he gives the instruction out of order, beginning with “devotion to the guru.”

children.text: athavā sarvārambhāṇāṃ lābhārthatvāt tatprādhānyajñāpanārthaṃ pūrvam ādau lābhā uddiṣṭā idānīṃ punaḥ sarve'pi lābhā upāyasādhyāste copāyā balahīnaiḥ puruṣairanuṣṭhātuṃ na śakyanta ityataḥ prādhānyajñāpanārthaṃ balānām ādau nirdeśam āha ||
children.translated_text: Or else, because all undertakings are for the sake of gain, the gains were first stated at the beginning in order to show their primacy. Now, again, all gains are accomplished through means, and those means cannot be practiced by people lacking powers; therefore, to show their primacy, he states the powers first.
The guru is the teacher, the instructor in the knowledge of the five topics.

children.text: tasya bhaktiḥ śraddhā sarvaduḥkhābhibhūtasya mamāyam eva trātety eṣā bhāvanā kāryā ||
children.translated_text: Devotion to him is faith. One must cultivate this conception: “For me, overcome by every suffering, he alone is the savior.”
And thus it has been said:

children.text: gurur devo guruḥ svāmī ityādi na ca kāraṇapravacanayor bhaktivirodhas tadanumatyaiva tayor bhaktisambhavāt ||
children.translated_text: “The guru is the god, the guru is the master,” and so forth. Nor is there any contradiction between devotion to the cause and to the doctrine, because devotion to those two is possible only with his permission.

children.text: yatas tu tayor bhaktiḥ kartavyeti nānumanyate sa gurur eva na bhavati ananugrahakāritvāt ||
children.translated_text: But since someone who does not permit devotion to those two is not to be revered, he is not a guru at all, because he does not bestow favor.

children.text: sā ca gurubhaktis tad anabhipretam pariharatotthānādikaṃ kurvatā ca satataṃ sevanīyā ||
children.translated_text: And that devotion to the guru is to be constantly practiced by avoiding what is displeasing to him and by doing such things as rising up in respect.

children.text: jñātvā tadabhiprāyam aśāstroktam api taddhitaṃ kartavyam ||
children.translated_text: Having understood his intention, even if it is not stated in śāstra, one should do what is beneficial to him.
And thus it has been said:
“Of one who knows the meaning of the text,” and so forth.

children.text: yad eva hi guror abhipretaṃ tad eva vihitaṃ śāstrānuktam api śreyaskari bhavati rāmasya mātṛvadhavat ||
children.translated_text: For whatever is intended by the guru, that alone is prescribed; even if not stated by scripture, it becomes conducive to welfare, as in the case of <s>Rāma</s> killing his mother.

children.text: guror vākyāni ca śraddheyāni anyathā doṣaśravaṇāt tattvajñānālābhaprasaṅgāc ca ||
children.translated_text: And the words of the guru are to be trusted; otherwise, because faults may be heard, and because the non-attainment of knowledge of reality would follow.

children.text: bhaktibalavihīno hi grahaṇādyupeto 'pi jñānāvalepenānyathā 'pi śāstrārthaṃ pratipadyata ity ato grahaṇādyupetasya bhaktir eva balam ||
children.translated_text: For one who lacks the strength of devotion, even if he is endowed with reception and the rest, interprets the meaning of the śāstra otherwise through pride in his knowledge; therefore, for one endowed with reception and the rest, devotion itself is strength.
Nor is there any contradiction with the commentary.

children.text: yato balam aṣṭāṅgaṃ brahmacaryam ity asyāyam arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For this is the meaning of the statement, “Strength is eight-limbed brahmacarya.”

children.text: aṣṭānāṃ grahaṇādīnām aṅgam aṣṭāṅgaṃ bhaktir evocyate vedāṅgavadarthāntarābhidhānāt ||
children.translated_text: “Eight-limbed” means an auxiliary to the eight things beginning with reception; devotion alone is so called, because another thing is denoted, as in the case of the Vedāṅgas.
That very thing, because it is the cause of brahmacarya, is called brahmacarya.

children.text: yadi punar yathāśrutārthaḥ syāt tadā vāsovidhānam ityādijñāpakābhidhānavirodhaḥ syād iti ||
children.translated_text: But if the meaning were just as heard, then there would be contradiction with the indicative statements such as the prescription concerning residence.
For one qualified for the injunction, he states the second strength.
“And serenity of the intellect.”
By the word “serenity of the intellect,” freedom from impurity is stated.

children.text: sati hi tasmin matiḥ prasannā bhavati ||
children.translated_text: For when that exists, the intellect becomes serene.

children.text: tathā ca balam akaluṣatvam iti bhāṣyam ||
children.translated_text: And likewise the commentary says: strength is freedom from impurity.

children.text: atrāpi tarhi spaṣṭābhidhānaṃ kim arthaṃ na kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: Then why was a clear statement not made here also?

children.text: matiprasādahetor anyasyāpy āśaucavyāmohādyabhāvasya balatvajñāpanārthaṃ pradhānāpekṣayā tv akaluṣatvam uktam ||
children.translated_text: In order to make known as strength the absence of other causes of disturbance, such as impurity and bewilderment, which are causes of serenity of the intellect; but with regard to the principal thing, freedom from impurity was stated.

children.text: caśabdaḥ pūrvoktabalasya vidyamānasyāpi caritārthatvāt tadbalatvaṃ prādhānyān na cintyata iti sūcayati
children.translated_text: The word “and” indicates that, although the previously mentioned strength is present, because it has fulfilled its purpose, its status as strength is not considered on account of primacy.

children.text: tac cākaluṣatvaṃ dvividhaṃ param aparaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: And that freedom from impurity is of two kinds, higher and lower.

children.text: tatra kaluṣatvabījasadbhāve 'py utpannakaluṣatvanirodhi yāvad anāgataṃ kaluṣaṃ notpadyate tāvatkālaṃ yad akaluṣatvaṃ tad aparaṃ yad bījakṣayād atyantanimittasadbhāve 'pi kaluṣaṃ notpadyate tat param iti ||
children.translated_text: There, although the seed of impurity exists, that freedom from impurity which suppresses arisen impurity, for as long as future impurity does not arise, is lower; that in which, because the seed has been destroyed, impurity does not arise even when all causes are present is higher.
For one qualified for yogic practice, he states the third strength.
“And likewise victory over the pairs of opposites.”

children.text: ādhyātmikādhibhautikādhidaivikāni duḥkhasādhanāni dvaṃdvāni teṣāṃ jayaḥ sahiṣṇutvaṃ dvaṃdvānabhibhāvyatvam ity arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The pairs of opposites are the causes of suffering that are internal, external, and divine; victory over them means endurance, the state of not being overcome by the pairs of opposites.
The word “likewise” has the sense of similarity.

children.text: yathā prāguktabale saty apy acaritārthavidhyadhikṛtasyākaluṣatvam eva balaṃ cintyate tathā baladvayasadbhāve 'py acaritārthaṃ dvaṃdvasahiṣṇutvam eva prādhānyena balaṃ cintyata iti ||
children.translated_text: Just as, even when the previously mentioned strength exists, freedom from impurity alone is considered as strength for one qualified for an injunction whose purpose has not been fulfilled, so too, even when the two strengths exist, endurance of the pairs of opposites alone, whose purpose has not been fulfilled, is considered strength in the primary sense.

children.text: tad api dvividhaṃ parāparabhedāt yat tāvad akṣapite pāpe yogakriyāyām abhiniviṣṭasya sādhakasya mṛdumadhyamaśītātapādibhir anubhāvyatvaṃ dhyānādyabhyāsas tad aparam ||
children.translated_text: That also is of two kinds, because of the distinction between higher and lower: when sin has not yet been exhausted, the practice of meditation and the like by a practitioner intent on yogic practice, while not being overcome by mild and moderate cold, heat, and so on, is lower.

children.text: yat kṣapite niḥśeṣapāpe guhādeśaṃ gatasyātitīvrair api śītādibhir anabhibhāvyasvalakṣaṇaṃ dvaṃdvasahiṣṇutvaṃ tat param ||
children.translated_text: When sin has been completely exhausted, the endurance of the pairs of opposites characterized by not being overcome even by extremely severe cold and the like, for one who has gone to a cave-place, is higher.

children.text: bhāṣyakṛtā tu param eva gomṛgadharmatvaṃ vyākhyātam ||
children.translated_text: But the author of the commentary explained only the higher condition of possessing the dharma of cattle and deer.

children.text: akaluṣatvavad abhyūhya śiṣyā aparaṃ gomṛgadharmitvaṃ pratipatsyanta ity abhiprāyavatā noktam iti ||
children.translated_text: His intention was that, inferring it as in the case of freedom from impurity, students will understand the lower condition of possessing the dharma of cattle and deer; therefore he did not state it.

children.text: sadāsmṛtyadhikṛtasya caturthaṃ balam āha dharmaś caiva iti ||
children.translated_text: For one qualified for constant recollection, he states the fourth strength: “and dharma alone.”
The word “alone” is restrictive.

children.text: yadā dharma evāvasthitas tadā balam ity arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The meaning is: when one is established in dharma alone, then there is strength.

children.text: īṣadadharmasadbhāve 'py avadhāraṇe nāsti doṣaḥ kṛṣṇabindusadbhāve śukla evāyaṃ paṭa iti yathā ||
children.translated_text: Even if a small amount of non-dharma is present, there is no fault in the restriction, just as one says, “This cloth is white alone,” even when a black spot is present.

children.text: caśabdaḥ pūrvoktabalatrayasadbhāve 'pi dharma evācaritārthatvena balam iti sūcayati ||
children.translated_text: The word “and” indicates that, even when the three previously mentioned strengths exist, dharma alone, because its purpose has not been fulfilled, is strength.

children.text: niṣṭhāyogayuktasya pañcamaṃ balam āha apramāda iti ||
children.translated_text: For one joined with the yoga of steadfastness, he states the fifth strength: “vigilance.”
Here a particular kind of knowledge itself is intended by “vigilance.”

children.text: tathā ca bhāṣyam asya tu jñānam asti yasmād āhāpramādī iti ||
children.translated_text: And likewise the commentary says: “But he has knowledge, because it says that he is vigilant.”

children.text: caśabdaḥ śarīrendriyadharmādharmavyāvṛttau satyām apramāda eva balam iti sūcayati balānāṃ nyūnādhikabhāvavyavacchedaṃ ceti ||
children.translated_text: The word “and” indicates that, when body, senses, dharma, and non-dharma have been excluded, vigilance alone is strength, and also excludes any lesser or greater status among the strengths.
This is the summing up: strength is fivefold.
“Remembered” shows that it has been stated by trustworthy persons.

children.text: nanu ca tatra balacintā yujyate yatra tat sampādya śatrukṣaya upapadyate ||
children.translated_text: But, one might object, discussion of strength is appropriate where, after that strength has been acquired, the destruction of enemies is possible.

children.text: atra punar mokṣaśāstre vītarāgasya niṣparigrahasya śatrava eva na vidyante kutaḥ tatkṣaya ity ato 'tra balacintānupapanneti ||
children.translated_text: Here, however, in a śāstra of liberation, for one free from passion and without possessions, there are no enemies at all; how then could there be their destruction? Therefore discussion of strength is inappropriate here.
This is not so.
Here too, since the destruction of enemies such as ignorance is possible for the practitioner, in order to teach that, he says:

children.text: ajñānahānir adharmasya iti prāpte chandobhaṅgaparihārārtham ajñānahānyadharmasyety uktam ||
children.translated_text: When “the destruction of ignorance, of non-dharma” was expected, “the destruction of ignorance, of non-dharma” was expressed in this form in order to avoid breaking the meter.
Because it is archaic usage, there is no fault.

children.text: ajñānaṃ ca vakṣyamāṇakaṃ tasya hāniḥ sabījasyātyantocchedaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Ignorance, which will be explained later, has its destruction, namely the complete eradication of it together with its seed.
Non-dharma too, which will be explained later, has its destruction, namely the complete eradication of it together with its effects.
As with non-dharma, the destruction of that which produces attachment has also been explained.
The word “and” serves to carry forward the word “destruction.”

children.text: cyuteḥ khalu vakṣyamāṇikāyāḥ saha bījenātyantocchedaś cyutihānir ity ucyate ||
children.translated_text: The destruction of falling away is said to be the complete eradication, together with its seed, of falling away, which will be explained later.
Because “of animality” is stated in the genitive case, it is connected with the immediately preceding word “destruction.”

children.text: ḍamarukamaṇinyāyena vā madhyoktaṃ hānipadaṃ cyutipaśutvābhyāṃ sambadhyate ||
children.translated_text: Or, by the ḍamaruka-jewel maxim, the word “loss” stated in the middle is connected with falling away and animality.
Or the word “and,” stated at the end of the word “causing attachment,” is carried over here.

children.text: sa na kevalaṃ hānipadānukarṣakaḥ śuddhīnāṃ nyūnādhikabhāvaṃ vyavacchinatti ||
children.translated_text: It not only draws forward the word “loss”; it also excludes any lesser or greater number of purifications.

children.text: paśutvasya māheśvaraiśvaryasambandhād ātyantiko nirodhaḥ paśutvahānir ity ucyate ||
children.translated_text: Because animality is connected with the lordly power of <s>Maheśvara</s>, its absolute cessation is called the loss of animality.
Thus the conclusion is that purification is fivefold.
The expression “are remembered” is for showing that this is stated by trustworthy authorities.

children.text: kiṃ punar etāḥ śatrunivṛttayo balāni cāvasthābhedabhinnasya sampadyante 'thaikāvasthasyeti ||
children.translated_text: But do these cessations of enemies and powers arise for one who is differentiated by different states, or for one in a single state?
Whence the doubt? Because both cases are seen, as in the case of <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s discus.

children.text: ucyate prāyeṇa tāvad avasthābhedabhinnasya yasmād avasthābhedam āha ||
children.translated_text: The answer is: for the most part, they belong to one differentiated by different states, since he states a difference of states.
The first state, indeed, was called the manifest state.
Why?

children.text: pāśupatye 'yam iti vyaktinimittatvāt bhasmasnānaśayanānusnānādibhir liṅgadhārīty upadeśād iti ||
children.translated_text: Because individuality is the basis for saying, “this one is in the Pāśupata discipline,” and because one who bears the marks is taught by such practices as bathing in ashes, sleeping on ashes, and bathing again.

children.text: dvitīyāvasthā tu jātyādivyakter ahetutvād avyaktāvasthety uktā ||
children.translated_text: But the second state is called the unmanifest state, because caste and the like are not the cause of manifestation.
Why?
Because of the instruction about an unmanifest mark and also the instruction to conceal knowledge and the like.
Again, the third state is called the state of conquest, because it has the conquest of the senses as its purpose.

children.text: devanityasvārthatve 'py asyā indriyajayārthataiva prādhānyenoktā sūtrāṇāṃ sambandhakathanadvāreṇācāryabhāṣyakṛteti ||
children.translated_text: Although it also has divinity, eternality, and self-benefit as its purposes, its purpose as conquest of the senses was stated as primary by the author of the teacher’s commentary, through the explanation of the connection of the sūtras.
The state whose purpose is the end of cutting off is called the state of cutting off.
The complete cessation of all activity of the practitioner is final completion.
The state characterized by that is called the state of final completion.

children.text: vyaktādiviśeṣaṇābhidhānādyūhādiśaktimatāṃ viśeṣapratipattir bhaviṣyatīty abhiprāyavatātrāvasthāgrahaṇaṃ na kṛtam iti ||
children.translated_text: Since, through the mention of qualifiers such as “manifest,” there will be a distinct understanding of those possessing powers such as reasoning, the word “state” was not used here by the author who had this intention.
The word “and” indicates the exclusion of a lesser or greater number.

children.text: pretonmattamūḍhāvasthāntarasadbhāvād adhikavyavacchedānupapattir iti cen na gopananiyamenāvyaktāvasthāyām evāntarbhāvāt ||
children.translated_text: If it is objected that exclusion of a greater number is impossible because there are other states such as those of a dead man, madman, and fool, no; because, by the rule of concealment, they are included precisely in the unmanifest state.

children.text: jayacchedāvasthayor apy avyaktāvasthātvaprasaṅga iti cen nānayor gopananiyamānabhyupagamān niṣṭhāvasthām anabhyupagamya siddhāvasthāṃ pañcamīm āhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: If it is objected that the states of conquest and cutting off would also become unmanifest states, no; because no rule of concealment is accepted for these two. Some, not accepting the state of final completion, speak of perfection as the fifth state.
He rejects that view by the restrictive particle itself.
“And final completion alone is here the fifth.”

children.text: ihety asmin pañcārthadarśane niṣṭhāvasthaiva pañcamī sūtraprāmāṇyāt pratīyate na siddhāvasthā ||
children.translated_text: “Here,” in this doctrine of the five topics, only the state of final completion is understood as the fifth on the authority of the sūtra, not a state of perfection.

children.text: tatra kṣapaṇīyaprāpaṇīyābhāvāt sādhakāvasthāś ceha nirūpyante na tato 'nyasyeti ||
children.translated_text: For in that state there is nothing to be destroyed or attained; and here the states of the practitioner are being examined, not that of anyone other than him.
Here someone says:
The attainment of a state by one who is not qualified is improper.

children.text: tatra tathā dvitīyādyavasthāprāptau jñānākaluṣatvādayo 'dhikāritvāpādakāḥ tathā prathamāvasthāprāptau ko hetur ity ucyate ||
children.translated_text: In that case, for the attainment of the second and following states, such qualities as unstained knowledge confer qualification. Likewise, when the first state is attained, what is the cause? This is answered:
Here too, initiation produced by a particular cause is the cause.
Therefore, in order to explain its cause, he says this:

children.text: atra vidyākalāpaśusaṃjñitaṃ vividhaṃ kāryaṃ dravyam ity ucyate ||
children.translated_text: Here the various effective substances called vidyā, kalā, and paśu are termed dravya.

children.text: tatra vidyā tāvac chiṣyagatā dīkṣāṅgaṃ yayā śiṣyo dīkṣādhikṛto bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Among these, vidyā is first the initiation-component residing in the disciple, by which the disciple becomes qualified for initiation.

children.text: yayā tv ācāryaḥ sampūrṇāṃ dīkṣāṃ nirvartayati sācāryagatā vidyā ||
children.translated_text: But that by which the teacher completes the full initiation is the vidyā residing in the teacher.
Kalā, such as darbha grass and the like, is a component of initiation.

children.text: uktaṃ hi darbhāḥ punar bhasma candanaṃ sūtram eva ca ||
children.translated_text: For it has been said: “Darbha grasses, then ashes, sandalwood, and also thread;

children.text: puṣpāṇi ca punar dhūpam eṣa kramaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and again flowers and incense: this sequence is remembered.”
The paśu, the one to be consecrated, is a brāhmaṇa.

children.text: itthaṃ vyākhyānakaraṇād upakaraṇāder api saṃgraha ity ato na saṃskārakārikāvirodhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because the explanation is made in this way, implements and the like are also included; therefore there is no contradiction with the Saṃskārakārikā.
The time is the forenoon.
The consecratory act concerning the causal form and the disciple is called the ritual action.
Its sequence is to be seen in the Saṃskārakārikā.

children.text: mūrtiśabdena yad upahārasūtre mahādevejyāsthānam ūrdhvaliṅgādilakṣaṇaṃ vyākhyātaṃ tatsamīpadakṣiṇabhūpradeśaḥ kuṭyādyavyavahito 'trābhipretaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By the word “form,” what was explained in the offering-sūtra as the place for worship of <s>Mahādeva</s>, characterized by the upright liṅga and so on, is intended here as the tract of ground to the south nearby, not separated by a hut and the like.
The guru is the teacher; he is twofold, by the division into higher and lower.
Among these, the lower is one endowed with the bounds of knowledge of the five topics.
And accordingly it has been said:
“He whose excellent intellect is intent on practice conforming to the śāstra, and who is skillful,

children.text: sa bhavati mataḥ kila satām ācāryo jñānahetuś ca ||
children.translated_text: is indeed considered by good people to be a teacher and a cause of knowledge.”
Likewise:

children.text: ācāre sthāpayan śiṣyān yasmād ācarati svayam
children.translated_text: “Because he establishes disciples in proper conduct and practices it himself,

children.text: ācinoti ca śāstrārthān ācāryas tena kīrtyate ||
children.translated_text: and because he gathers up the meanings of the śāstra, therefore he is called ācārya.”

children.text: tasyādhiṣṭhātā bhagavān maheśvaraḥ paro gurus tathā caivaṃ varṇite nimittam apy atra nānuktaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: The presiding lord over him is the blessed <s>Maheśvara</s>, the higher guru. Thus, when it is explained in this way, the cause too is not left unstated here.
The word “and” indicates the exclusion of a lesser or greater number.
The word “alone” restrictively establishes the primacy of the guru.
“Here” is a reference to his own doctrine.
“As the fifth” is the conclusion.

children.text: athavā eva iha padayoḥ pāṭhaviparyayaṃ kṛtvānyathārthaḥ pradarśyate ||
children.translated_text: Or else, by reversing the reading of the words “alone” and “here,” another meaning is shown.
Only here, in this very Pāśupata doctrine, are such requisites of initiation found, and not elsewhere.

children.text: tataś ca niṣpādyā dīkṣāpy atraiva viśiṣṭāsti nānyatrety uktaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: And from this it is stated that the initiation to be accomplished is specifically distinguished here alone, and not elsewhere.

children.text: atha kiṃ kāraṇaviśeṣair eveyaṃ dīkṣā viśiṣyate na kiṃ tarhi phalaviśeṣair api ||
children.translated_text: Now, is this initiation distinguished only by particular causes, or rather also by particular results?
Since it is for that purpose that he says this:

children.text: tatra pañcapadārthaviṣayaṃ samāsavistaravibhāgaviśeṣopasaṃhāranigamanatas tattvajñānaṃ prathamo vidyālābho jñānam iti cocyate ||
children.translated_text: There, the first acquisition of knowledge, called knowledge, is the knowledge of reality concerning the five topics by way of summary, expansion, division, distinction, recapitulation, and conclusion.

children.text: teṣāṃ samāsādīnāṃ svarūpaṃ yady api śrīmatācāryeṇa bhāṣyāvasāne prakaṭitaṃ tathāpi leśatas tadbhāṣyavivaraṇārtham asmābhir apy ucyate ||
children.translated_text: Although the nature of those, the summary and the rest, has been made clear by the venerable teacher at the end of the commentary, nevertheless we too state it briefly for the purpose of explaining that commentary.
There, the statement of the topics is the summary.
That has been expressed by the words beginning with 'now,' 'sound,' and so on, down to the end of suffering.
The detailed statement, on the basis of means of knowledge, of what has been stated is the expansion.
For example, 'the Lord, having equipped,' and so on.
The means of knowledge too are referred to by the word expansion, since they serve as its instruments.
The statement, according to what is possible, of the difference between properties and property-bearers through definition is division.
Everywhere also, the term abhidhāna is so called because it is expressed.
A derivation from the action should be understood.
There, first the division of the end of suffering is stated.
The end of suffering is the removal of all suffering.
It is twofold: without self-nature and with self-nature.

children.text: tatrānātmakaḥ sarvaduḥkhānām atyantocchedaḥ sātmakas tu maheśvaraiśvaryalakṣaṇā siddhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Among these, the one without self-nature is the absolute destruction of all sufferings, while the one with self-nature is siddhi characterized by the sovereignty of <s>Maheśvara</s>.
That is of two forms: knowledge-power and action-power.
There, the power that is knowledge itself is knowledge-power.

children.text: sā khalv ekāpi satī samastavyastaviṣayabhedāt pañcadhoktā darśanaśravaṇetyādinā brahmāder ivopacaritasarvajñatvapratiṣedhārtham ||
children.translated_text: Although it is one, it is taught as fivefold, by the terms seeing, hearing, and so on, because of the distinction between collective and separate objects, in order to deny a merely figurative omniscience such as that of <s>Brahmā</s> and others.

children.text: kriyāhetuḥ śaktiḥ kriyāśaktiḥ sā trividhā manojavitvādibhedā ||
children.translated_text: The power that is the cause of action is action-power; it is threefold, divided into swiftness of mind and the like.

children.text: tatra niratiśayaṃ śīghrakāritvaṃ manojavitvaṃ karmādinirapekṣasyecchayaivānantararūpakartṛtvādhiṣṭhātṛtvaṃ kāmarūpitvaṃ saṃbhṛtakāyendriyasyāpi niratiśayaiśvaryasambandhitvaṃ vikaraṇadharmitvaṃ ceti ||
children.translated_text: There, unsurpassed quickness in acting is swiftness of mind; being the maker and controller of immediately assumed forms merely by wish, without dependence on karma and the like, is taking forms at will; and being connected with unsurpassed sovereignty even when one has a body and senses assembled is the state of being without organs.

children.text: yadā ceyaṃ dvirūpā siddhiḥ prāpyate tadā daśa siddhilakṣaṇāny avaśyatvādīni patitvāntāni bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: And when this twofold siddhi is attained, then the ten marks of siddhi, beginning with independence and ending with lordship, necessarily arise.
There, unsurpassed non-dependence on another is independence.
Now, what is this so-called independence?

children.text: vaśyatvamalanivṛttāvaśyatvākhyaḥ puruṣe 'vasthito dharmo 'bhivyajyate paṭe śuklatāvad ity eke ||
children.translated_text: Some say that, when the impurity of subjection has ceased, a property situated in the person called independence is manifested, like whiteness in a cloth.

children.text: tac cāyuktam aiśvaryābhivyakteḥ pratiṣiddhatvād anātmakasya ca dharmasyābhivyaktyanupapatter anyathānātmakatvavirodhaḥ syād yadā guṇair yukta ityādi bhāṣyavirodhāc ca nāvasthitābhivyaktiḥ kiṃ tv aiśvaryasambandha eva parādhīnatvanivartakatvād avaśyatvam ucyate ||
children.translated_text: But that is not reasonable, because the manifestation of sovereignty has been denied; because the manifestation of a property without self-nature is impossible, since otherwise there would be contradiction of its being without self-nature; and because it contradicts the commentary passage beginning 'when he is joined with the qualities.' Therefore it is not the manifestation of something already situated there; rather, the very connection with sovereignty is called independence, since it removes dependence on another.

children.text: athavā yadā guṇair yuktas tadā sa evātathābhūtapūrvas tathā bhavati sarpaśikyādivat tasya bhāvas tatsvarūpam avaśyatvaṃ bhedanocyate vyavahārārtham ity evam anāveśyatvādiṣv api vicāro draṣṭavyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Or else, when he is joined with the qualities, then that very one, who was not formerly such, becomes such, like a snake, a sling, and so forth. Its state, its own nature, is called independence; the difference is stated for the sake of ordinary usage. In this same way the analysis should also be understood in regard to non-possession and the others.

children.text: satkāryavicāre cāyaṃ vistārito mayā teneha na pratanyate ||
children.translated_text: And I have explained this at length in the discussion of the existent effect, so it is not expanded here.

children.text: sattvāntarānabhibhāvyajñānasambandhitvam anāveśyatvaṃ sattvāntarādhīnajīvitarahitatvam avadhyatvam samastabhayātikrāntatvam abhayatvam aiśvaryeṇa nityasambandhitvam akṣayatvaṃ kāyendriyavaikalyaphalenātyantāsambandhitvam ajaratvaṃ prāṇādiviyogajaduḥkhāsaṃsparśitvam amaratvaṃ sarvatrābhipretārtheṣu pravartamānasya maheśvareṇāpy apratibandhadharmitvam apratīghātaḥ sarvapaśubhyo 'bhyadhikatvam aiśvaryātiśayān mahattvaṃ sarvapaśvādikāryasvāmitvaṃ patitvam iti ||
children.translated_text: Being connected with knowledge that cannot be overpowered by another being is non-possession; being free from life dependent on another being is invulnerability; having passed beyond all fear is fearlessness; being eternally connected with sovereignty is inexhaustibility; absolute non-connection with the result consisting in defect of body and senses is agelessness; being untouched by suffering born of separation from breath and the like is immortality; being of a nature that is not obstructed even by <s>Maheśvara</s> when acting everywhere toward desired objects is non-obstruction; superiority over all bound souls because of an excess of sovereignty is greatness; and mastery over all effects beginning with bound souls is lordship.

children.text: yad asvatantraṃ tat sarvakāryaṃ tasya vibhāga ucyate vidyā kalā paśuś ceti ||
children.translated_text: Whatever is not independent is all an effect; its division is now stated as vidyā, kalā, and paśu.
There, vidyā is a quality of the bound soul, stated from the standpoint of one's own śāstra.
From the standpoint of the <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> system, it is like a substance.
It is twofold, according to the difference between the nature of cognition and non-cognition.

children.text: tatrābodhasvabhāvā dharmādilakṣaṇā vidyāntarbhāvakaraṇād avidyātmakasya vidyāntarbhāve kalāder apy antarbhāvaḥ syād iti ||
children.translated_text: There, vidyā whose nature is non-cognition is characterized by dharma and the like, because these are included within vidyā; for if what is of the nature of avidyā were included within vidyā, then kalā and the rest too would have to be included.

children.text: bodhasvabhāvā tu viṣayabhedāc caturdhā pañcadhā coktā ||
children.translated_text: But vidyā whose nature is cognition is said to be fourfold and fivefold because of differences in object.

children.text: svarūpatas tu dvidhā vivekavṛttiḥ sāmānyavṛttiś ceti ||
children.translated_text: In its own nature, however, it is twofold: the discriminating mode and the general mode.

children.text: tatra vivekavṛttiḥ prāyeṇopadeśavyaṅgyā na ca tatra samākhyāntaram asti ||
children.translated_text: There, the discriminating mode is for the most part made manifest by instruction, and there is no further designation for it.

children.text: vidyaiva hi viśeṣasamākhyā sāmānyavṛttis tu pramāṇamātravyaṅgyā cittam ity uktā ||
children.translated_text: For vidyā itself is the particular designation; but the general mode, made manifest merely by a means of knowledge, is called citta.

children.text: anayor bhedaṣ ṭīkāntare mayā darśita neha pradarśyate ||
children.translated_text: The difference between these two has been shown by me in another commentary; it is not displayed here.
Kalā is unconscious while not being dependent on conscious beings.
It too is twofold: that called effect and that called instrument.

children.text: tatra kāryākhyā daśavidhā pṛthivyaptejovāvyākāśagandharasarūpasparśaśabdalakṣaṇā karaṇākhyā tu trayodaśavidhā pañca karmendriyāṇi pañca buddhīndriyāṇy antaḥkaraṇatrayaṃ ceti ||
children.translated_text: Among these, what is called the effect is tenfold, characterized as earth, water, fire, air, ether, smell, taste, form, touch, and sound; but what is called the instrument is thirteenfold, namely the five organs of action, the five organs of cognition, and the threefold internal organ.
A paśu is one connected with paśutva, the state of being bound like a paśu.
That too is twofold: with stain and without stain.
Among these, the stained one, connected with body and senses, is fourteenfold.

children.text: uktaṃ hi daivam aṣṭavidhaṃ jñeyaṃ tairyagyonaṃ ca pañcadhā
children.translated_text: For it has been said: The divine is to be known as eightfold, and the animal womb as fivefold;

children.text: parvam ekaṃ tu mānuṣyam etat saṃsāramaṇḍalam ||
children.translated_text: the human is one category: this is the circle of saṃsāra.

children.text: iti nirañjanas tu trividhaḥ saṃhṛtaḥ kaivalyagato niṣṭhāyogayuktaś ceti ||
children.translated_text: Thus the stainless one is threefold: withdrawn, gone to isolation, and joined with the yoga of completion.

children.text: samastasṛṣṭisaṃhārānugrahakāri kāraṇaṃ tasyaikasyāpi guṇadharmabhedād vibhāga ukto 'nyatpatitvam ityādinā ||
children.translated_text: The cause that effects the whole creation, withdrawal, and favor, though it is one, is said to be divided according to distinctions of qualities and properties, by the words beginning with 'being lord of another.'

children.text: niratiśayadṛkkriyāśaktiḥ patitvaṃ tenaiśvaryeṇa nityasambandhitvaṃ sattvam anāgantukaiśvaryatvam ādyatvaṃ samastajanmarahitatvam ajātatvaṃ mahāsṛṣṭisaṃhārakartṛtvaṃ bhavodbhavatvaṃ paramotkṛṣṭaṃ guṇadharmanimittanāmābhidheyatvaṃ vāmatvaṃ duḥkhāntanimittadharmotpādakanāmābhidheyatvaṃ vā svecchayaivāśeṣakāryotpattyādikāraṇasvabhāvaḥ krīḍā taddharmitvaṃ devatvaṃ siddhasādhakapaśubhyaḥ paratvaṃ jyeṣṭhatvaṃ sargādāv api rutabhayasaṃyojakatvaṃ rudratvam karmādinirapekṣasya svecchayaivāśeṣakāryakartṛtvaṃ kāmitvaṃ śamasukhanirvāṇakaratvaṃ śaṃkaratvam antarasṛṣṭyām api saṃhārakartṛtvaṃ kālatvaṃ kāryakāraṇākhyānāṃ kalānāṃ sthānaśarīrādibhāvena saṃyojakatvaṃ kalavikaraṇatvaṃ dharmādibalānāṃ yatheṣṭaṃ vṛttilābhalopākṣepakartṛtvaṃ balapramathanatvaṃ sarvadevamānuṣatiraścāṃ ratirañjanādhivāsanākartṛtvaṃ sarvabhūtadamanatvaṃ sakalaniṣkalāvasthāyās tulyaśaktitvaṃ manomanastvaṃ sukhakarānantaśarīrādhiṣṭātṛtvam aghoratvaṃ duḥkhakarānantaśarīrādhiṣṭātṛtvaṃ ghorataratvaṃ sarvavidyādikāryāṇāṃ vyāptādhiṣṭhātṛtvaṃ pūraṇaṃ yathepsitānantaśarīrādikaraṇaśaktiḥ pauruṣyam ||
children.translated_text: Patitva, lordship, is unsurpassed power of vision and action. Sattva is eternal connection with that sovereignty. Ādyatva is the possession of sovereignty that has not newly arrived. Ajātatva is complete absence of all birth. Bhavodbhavatva is being the maker of the great creation and withdrawal. Vāmatva is being denoted by a name based on an especially exalted quality or property, or else by a name that produces the property that is the cause of the end of suffering. Krīḍā is the nature of being, by one's own will alone, the cause of the origination and so on of all effects. Devatva is possession of that property. Jyeṣṭhatva is superiority to siddhas, sādhakas, and paśus. Rudratva is causing the connection of cries and fear even at the beginning of creation. Kāmitva is making all effects by one's own will alone, without dependence on karma and the like. Śaṅkaratva is bringing peace, happiness, and nirvāṇa. Kālatva is being the destroyer even in the inner creation. Kalavikaraṇatva is connecting the kalās called effects and causes as places, bodies, and so forth. Balapramathanatva is causing the obtaining, loss, and casting down of the functions of powers such as dharma as one wishes. Sarvabhūtadamanatva is causing delight, coloring, and indwelling in all gods, humans, and animals. Manomanastva is equal power in the state with parts and without parts. Aghoratva is presiding over endless bodies that bring happiness. Ghorataratva is presiding over endless bodies that bring suffering. Pūraṇa is pervasive overlordship of all effects such as the sciences. Pauruṣya is the power to produce endless bodies and the like as desired.
Both of these are called the <s>Bhagavat</s>'s puruṣatva.
Mahattva is being greater, more excellent, and distinct from all paśus and the rest; devatva has been explained before.
Oṃkāratva is being the single object of meditation that causes the end of suffering.
Ṛṣitva is the power of action, while vipratva is the power of knowledge.

children.text: anayor āśrayavyāpitvānantaviṣayatvaniratiśayatvajñāpanārthaṃ tadāśrayo bhagavān mahān ity uktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In order to make known that these two have their support as all-pervasive, infinite in object, and unsurpassed, it was said that the <s>Bhagavat</s>, their support, is great.

children.text: sarvadā sarvatrāvicalitasvabhāvena vartamāno bhagavān eṣa ity ucyate ||
children.translated_text: This <s>Bhagavat</s>, existing always and everywhere with an unshaken nature, is called 'this one.'

children.text: guṇadharmadvāreṇa vācaḥ pravartante yasmād atas tadvyatiriktas tadaviśeṣitaś ca bhagavān viśuddha ity ucyate ||
children.translated_text: Since words proceed through qualities and properties, the <s>Bhagavat</s>, being distinct from them and not qualified by them, is called pure.
In the supreme cause, endowed with eternal sovereignty that has not newly arrived,

children.text: yatra vāco nivartante vāgviśuddhaḥ sa kīrtitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: where words turn back, he is called purified of speech.

children.text: kṣaṇaikam api yas tatra prāpnoty ekāgratāṃ yatiḥ
children.translated_text: The ascetic who there obtains one-pointedness even for a single moment,
burning up all karmas, would attain union with <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: sarvaiśvaryapradātṛtvaṃ maheśvaratvaṃ samastakāryaviṣayaṃ prabhutvam īśatvaṃ sarvavidyāviṣayaṃ prabhutvam īśānatvaṃ sarvabhūtaviṣayaṃ prabhutvam īśvaratvam ||
children.translated_text: Maheśvaratva is being the giver of all sovereignty. Īśatva is mastery over all effects. Īśānatva is mastery over all sciences. Īśvaratva is mastery over all beings.

children.text: prakramāpekṣaḥ khalv evam īśādiśabdānām arthaḥ pradarśito 'nyathā punar ekārthatvam eveti ||
children.translated_text: Thus the meaning of words such as īśa has been shown with reference to the immediate topic; otherwise, they simply have one and the same meaning.

children.text: brahmagrahaṇasyodāharaṇārthatvād aśeṣapativiṣayaprabhutvam adhipatitvaṃ bṛṃhaṇabṛhattvaṃ brahmatvaṃ paripūrṇaparitṛptatvaṃ śivatvam iti ||
children.translated_text: Because the mention of <s>Brahmā</s> is by way of example, adhipatitva is lordship over all lords; brahmatva is expanding and greatness; śivatva is being completely full and satisfied.

children.text: evaṃ suniścitāḥ khalv ime guṇadharmāḥ parameśvarasyopahārakāle gāyatā bhāvayitavyāḥ satataṃ vā japaṃ ca kurvatā vibhaktyupasarganipātakriyāpadānām arthaiḥ saha cintanīyās tato 'cireṇaiva kālena śuddhivṛddhī bhavataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, certainly, these well-ascertained qualities and properties of <s>Parameśvara</s> are to be contemplated when one sings at the time of offering, or constantly by one who performs recitation; they are to be reflected on together with the meanings of case endings, prefixes, particles, and verbs. Then, in a short time, purification and increase arise.
And these are to be known by one's own self-experience.
An injunction is the activity of the practitioner whose object is dharma.
It is twofold: principal and subordinate.

children.text: tatrāvyavadhānena dharmahetur yo vidhiḥ sa pradhānabhūtaś caryeti vakṣyate ||
children.translated_text: Among these, the injunction that is the cause of dharma without mediation is principal; it will be called conduct.
But what supports conduct is subordinate, such as subsequent bathing and the like.

children.text: tatra bhuktocchiṣṭādinimittāyogyatāpratyayanivṛttyarthaṃ liṅgābhivyaktyarthaṃ ca yat snānaṃ yat kaluṣanivṛttyarthaṃ tad upasparśanam ||
children.translated_text: There, the bathing that is for removing the cognition of unfitness caused by eating leftovers and the like, and for manifesting the liṅga, is snāna; that which is for removing impurity is upasparśana.

children.text: etad ubhayam apy ajapataiveśvaraniyogam anusaṃdhāya saṃsāradoṣaṃ bhāvayatā gurulaghubhāvaṃ ca paryālocya bhasmanaiva kartavyam ||
children.translated_text: Both of these should be performed only with ash, while not doing japa, attending to the command of <s>Īśvara</s>, contemplating the defect of saṃsāra, and considering whether the occasion is major or minor.
Wearing the nirmālya too supports conduct, through the manifestation of the liṅga and the increase of devotion.

children.text: vicārya kāraṇanirmālyaṃ niṣparigrahaṃ paraṃ kṛtaṃ gṛhītvā saṃyatātmanā kāraṇaṃ praṇamyānujñāṃ prārthayet tataḥ prasannamukhaṃ bhagavantaṃ svanirmālyaṃ nirmalīkaraṇāya prayacchantaṃ dhyātvā mahāprasāda ity abhisaṃdhāya bhaktyaiva śirasi dhārayet ||
children.translated_text: Having considered the nirmālya of the cause to be supreme and without possession, one should take it with a restrained self, bow to the cause, and ask permission. Then, meditating on the gracious-faced <s>Bhagavat</s> as giving his own nirmālya for purification, and intending, 'This is great prasāda,' one should wear it on the head with devotion alone.
Likewise, dwelling in the sanctuary too supports conduct.
And so it is said:

children.text: dharmakṣetraṃ paraṃ hy etac chivāyatanaṃ bhuvi
children.translated_text: This sanctuary of <s>Śiva</s> on earth is indeed the supreme field of dharma;

children.text: vidhibījasya sā bhūmis tatra vaptam mahāphalam ||
children.translated_text: that ground is the seed-bed of the seed of injunction; what is sown there has a great fruit.
For a hundred hastas and a little more from the liṅga, the field of <s>Śiva</s> extends all around;
for living beings, death there is a cause of union with <s>Śiva</s>.
The passage beginning 'whether in a village or...' is similar.
Prāṇāyāma is for destroying the impurity not destroyed by upasparśana.
Prāṇāyāma is the restraint of the movement of the air in the abdomen.

children.text: tatropaspṛśya kāraṇatīrthakaragurūn anupraṇamya prāṅmukha udaṅmukho vā padmakasvastikādīnām anyatamaṃ yathāsukham āsanaṃ baddhvā kṛtam unnataṃ ca kṛtvā śanaiḥ saṃyatāntaḥkaraṇena recakādīn kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: There, after performing upasparśana and bowing in succession to the cause, the tīrthas, and the gurus, facing east or north, having assumed as comfortably as possible one among the postures such as padmaka or svastika, and having made the body straight and raised, one should slowly perform recaka and the others with the inner organ restrained.
Even when there is no impurity, one should perform it daily in order to bring about extreme purity of the mind and for the sake of practice.
For it is said:

children.text: prāṇāyāmair dahed doṣān dhāraṇābhiś ca kilbiṣam
children.translated_text: By prāṇāyāmas one should burn faults, and by dhāraṇās sin;
by pratyāhāra, sense objects, and by meditation, the qualities that are not of the Lord.
For a twice-born man joined with prāṇāyāma and restrained in self,

children.text: sarve doṣāḥ praṇaśyanti sattvasthaś caiva jāyate ||
children.translated_text: all faults perish, and he becomes established in sattva.

children.text: jalabindukuśāgreṇa māse māse ca yaḥ pibet
children.translated_text: If someone were to drink, month by month, with a drop of water on the tip of kuśa grass,
for a full hundred years, that is equal to a single prāṇāyāma.
Because one whose self has been purified by prāṇāyāma sees that supreme reality,

children.text: tasmāt kiṃcit paraṃ nāsti prāṇāyāmād iti śrutiḥ ||
children.translated_text: there is nothing higher than prāṇāyāma, according to scripture.
Japa should be performed for destroying the impurity not destroyed by that.

children.text: tṛtīyacaturthayor anyatarasmin brahmaṇi prayatnaniruddhaṃ cittaṃ sampūrṇākṣarānubodhena tadarthānubodhena vā punaḥ punaḥ saṃcārayed iti ||
children.translated_text: In either the third or fourth <s>brahman</s>, one should again and again direct the mind, restrained by effort, either through understanding the complete syllables or through understanding their meaning.

children.text: evaṃ ca prāyaścittāntaram utsūtratvān na kartavyam iti ||
children.translated_text: And thus no other expiation should be performed, because it would go beyond the sūtra.

children.text: nanu ca trikasya kaluṣanivṛttyartham evābhidhānaṃ vyabhicārāntareṣu punaḥ kiṃ prāyaścittam ||
children.translated_text: But, one may object, the statement of the triad is only for the removal of impurity. In the case of other transgressions, what expiation is there?

children.text: na caitad vācyaṃ yater apramattasya sarvadaiva saṃyatatvād asambhavī vyabhicāra iti kāmādivyabhicāreṇa samānatvāt trikasyāpy anārambhaprasaṅgo vā ||
children.translated_text: And it should not be said that transgression is impossible for an ascetic who is heedful, because he is always restrained; for the triad too is the same as transgression through desire and so on, or else there would be the consequence that the triad would not be undertaken.
Moreover, because of the power of adharma, transgression is possible even for one who knows.
And it is said, 'Even while understanding, he is carried away,' and so on.
And because violence is unavoidable.
For it is said:

children.text: ahṇā rātryā ca yāñ jantūn nihanty ajñānato yatiḥ
children.translated_text: The living beings that an ascetic kills unknowingly by day and by night,

children.text: teṣāṃ snātvā viśuddhyarthaṃ prāṇāyāmān ṣaḍ ācaret ||
children.translated_text: for their purification, after bathing, he should perform six prāṇāyāmas.
This means every day.

children.text: atraike sarvavyabhicāreṣu trikam eva kartavyam iti manyante ||
children.translated_text: Here some think that in all transgressions the triad alone should be performed.

children.text: vayaṃ tu paśyāmaḥ kaluṣanivṛttyartham eva trikaṃ kartavyam ||
children.translated_text: But we hold that the triad should be performed only for the removal of impurity.

children.text: bhāṣyasyāpi tathaiva śrutatvān nādṛṣṭārtham adṛṣṭaśuddheś cāniścayāt trikānuparamaprasaṅgaḥ syāt tasmāt kaluṣanivṛttau pūrvakṛtādharmakṣapaṇavad vyabhicārakṛtādharmakṣapaṇārtham api vidhyācaraṇam eva kartavyam ||
children.translated_text: For the commentary too is heard in just that way, and not for an unseen purpose; and because purification of the unseen is uncertain, there would be the consequence that the triad would never cease. Therefore, when impurity is removed, just as prescribed conduct is to be performed for the destruction of previously committed adharma, so too it should be performed for the destruction of adharma committed through transgression.

children.text: tathā ca sūtraṃ bhūyas tapaś caret iti ||
children.translated_text: And accordingly the sūtra says, 'He should perform austerity again.'
<s>Manu</s> also says:

children.text: yat kiṃcid enaḥ kurvanti vāṅmanomūrtibhir janāḥ
children.translated_text: Whatever sin people commit by speech, mind, or body,

children.text: tat sarvaṃ nirṇudanty āśu tapasaiva tapodhanāḥ ||
children.translated_text: all that the rich in austerity quickly drive away by austerity alone.
Even great sinners, and the rest who do what ought not to be done,
are released from sin through austerity that has been well practiced.
Likewise, by the illustrious author of the commentary too an indicating statement has been made:

children.text: tapobhir āryā nirṇudanti pāpaṃ dhyānopayogāt kṣapayanti puṇyam
children.translated_text: By austerities the noble drive away sin; through the application of meditation they destroy merit.

children.text: te nirmalās tattvavido viśuddhā gacchanti mokṣaṃ hy ubhayor abhāvāt ||
children.translated_text: They, stainless, knowers of reality, and purified, go to liberation, because both are absent.

children.text: na cāyaṃ niyamaḥ puṇyakṣaya eva dhyānāt kiṃtu pāpakṣayo 'pi ||
children.translated_text: And this is not a restriction that only merit is destroyed by meditation; rather, sin too is destroyed.
For another indicating statement is given in that very place:
By meditation he burns up everything that is the support of activity producing merit and sin;

children.text: puṇyapāpaphale dagdhe svāmī tasya na vidyate ||
children.translated_text: when the fruits of merit and sin are burnt, he has no master over him.
So it says.

children.text: evaṃ tarhy anarthakaṃ vidhyanuṣṭhānam iti cen nānena vidhinā rudrasamīpaṃ gatveti pravacanād vidhyanuṣṭhānavikalasya yogānuṣṭhānasāmarthyābhāvāt ||
children.translated_text: If, then, the performance of injunctions is useless, no: because the teaching says, 'having gone near <s>Rudra</s> by this injunction,' and because one who lacks performance of injunctions lacks the capacity for performance of yoga.
And so elsewhere too it is said:

children.text: dharmaḥ prayatnataḥ kāryo yoginā tu viśeṣataḥ
children.translated_text: Dharma should be practiced with effort, especially by a yogin;

children.text: nāsti dharmād ṛte yoga iti yogavido viduḥ iti ||
children.translated_text: the knowers of yoga know that there is no yoga apart from dharma.

children.text: tasmād upasparśanādibhiḥ prasannaṃ cittaṃ kṛtvā sarvasyādharmasya kṣapaṇārthaṃ vidhiyogānuṣṭhānam evātyantādyabhiyogena kartavyaṃ na prāyaścittāntaram iti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, after making the mind clear by upasparśana and the like, for the destruction of all adharma one must perform precisely the practice of injunction and yoga with the utmost, initial exertion, and not another expiation.

children.text: tathā daśāhiṃsādayo yamāś caryānugrāhakā yadā tadā vidhyantarbhūtā yadā tu yogakriyānugrāhakās tadā yogāntarbhūtā iti ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, when the ten restraints such as non-violence are supports of conduct, then they are included within injunction; but when they are supports of yogic practice, then they are included within yoga.

children.text: tatra vākkāyamanobhiḥ paraduḥkhānutpādanam ahiṃsā indriyasaṃyamo brahmacaryaṃ dharmasādhanānaṅgavacanapratiṣedhaḥ satyaṃ varṇāśramibhiḥ saha dṛṣṭārthasaṃgatipratiṣedho 'saṃvyavahāraḥ dharmasādhanāṅgād abhyadhikasya nyāyato 'py asvīkaraṇam anyāyatas tu dharmasādhanāṅgasyāpy asvīkaraṇaṃ cāsteyaṃ parair apakṛtasyāpy amlānacittatvam akrodhaḥ vākkāyamanobhir gurau hitabhāvenaiva vartanaṃ guruśuśrūṣā kāyāntaḥkaraṇātmaśuddhiḥ śaucaṃ svavṛttyaivopārjitānnasya vidhiyogānuṣṭhānāvirodhenābhyavaharaṇam āhāralāghavam ||
children.translated_text: There, non-production of suffering for others by speech, body, and mind is non-violence; restraint of the senses is brahmacarya; prohibition of speech that is not a limb of the means to dharma is truth; prohibition of association for visible worldly ends with members of the varṇas and āśramas is non-transaction; not accepting, even justly, anything beyond what is a limb of the means to dharma, and not accepting even a limb of the means to dharma unjustly, is non-stealing; keeping the mind unwithered even toward one who has done harm is absence of anger; behaving toward the teacher by speech, body, and mind only with a beneficial disposition is service to the teacher; purification of body, internal organ, and self is purity; eating food obtained by one's own livelihood only insofar as it does not conflict with the performance of prescribed injunction and yoga is lightness of diet.

children.text: aṣṭau grāsā muner iti kecit tan neṣṭaṃ vidhiyogānuṣṭhānavirodhaprasaṅgāt ||
children.translated_text: Some say, 'Eight mouthfuls for the sage.' That is not accepted, because it would entail conflict with the performance of prescribed injunction and yoga.

children.text: savyañjanāśanodakābhyāṃ koṣṭhasya bhāgatrayaṃ pūrayitvā caturthaṃ bhāgaṃ vāyoḥ saṃcaraṇārtham avaśeṣayed ity anye ||
children.translated_text: Others say that, having filled three parts of the belly with food together with condiments and water, one should leave the fourth part for the movement of wind.
That alone is accepted, because there is no conflict.

children.text: atra ca pañcavidhabhaikṣābhidhāyakaṃ vākyaṃ caren mādhukarīm ityādy avirodhena vyākhyeyam ||
children.translated_text: And here the statement that sets forth the fivefold alms, beginning 'one should practice the bee-like alms round,' is to be explained in a way that is not contradictory.
Constant effort in the performance of injunction and yoga as prescribed is vigilance.
And this is the principal yama.
And so it has been said:
Listen to the real nature of the dharma of ascetics, according to its virtue and fault:

children.text: apramādāt parā siddhiḥ pramādān narakaṃ dhruvam ||
children.translated_text: from vigilance comes the supreme accomplishment; from negligence, hell is certain.
Thus.
Even residence is only an injunction concerning a subsidiary quality, because it supports conduct through the production of knowledge.
Yoga is the relation of the person to <s>Īśvara</s> through the mind.
It is twofold: characterized by activity and characterized by the cessation of activity.
There, what is characterized by activity consists of recitation, control, concentration, meditation, and recollection.
We shall explain it.
What is characterized by cessation of activity is also denoted by words such as atigati.
The distinctiveness is the statement of the superiority of these over the categories taught in other śāstras.

children.text: tathāhi śāstrāntare duḥkhanivṛttir eva duḥkhāntaḥ iha tu paramaiśvaryaprāptiś ca ||
children.translated_text: For example, in another śāstra the end of suffering is only the cessation of suffering; but here it is also the attainment of supreme sovereignty.

children.text: tathānyatrābhūtvā bhāvi kāryam iha tu nityaṃ paśvādi ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, elsewhere an effect is something that comes to be after not having existed; but here paśu and the like are eternal.

children.text: tathānyatrāsvatantraṃ pradhānādi kāraṇam iha tu svatantro bhagavān eva ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, elsewhere a cause such as pradhāna is non-independent; but here the independent <s>Bhagavat</s> alone is the cause.

children.text: tathānyatra kaivalyābhyudayaphalo yogaḥ iha tu paramaduḥkhāntaphalaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, elsewhere yoga has isolation or prosperity as its fruit; but here its fruit is the supreme end of suffering.

children.text: tathānyatrāvartakaḥ svargādiphalo vidhir iha tv anāvartako rudrasamīpādiphala iti ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, elsewhere injunction has a fruit such as heaven, from which there is return; but here it has a fruit such as nearness to <s>Rudra</s>, from which there is no return.

children.text: padārthānāṃ samāptisaṃhāras tatra duḥkhakāryakāraṇavidhīnām iti śabdena samāptir uktā ||
children.translated_text: The conclusion is the completion and summing up of the categories; there the completion of suffering, effect, cause, and injunction is stated by the word 'iti'.
But that of yoga is stated by the word 'tu'.

children.text: samāptānāṃ niḥśeṣīkaraṇārthaṃ prāsaṅgikasaṃśayanivṛttyarthaṃ ca dharmāntarābhidhānaṃ nigamanam ||
children.translated_text: A conclusion is the statement of another dharma in order to make what has been completed exhaustive and to remove incidental doubt.
Others say that it is for showing that it forms one sentence with the matter promised at the outset.

children.text: tad evaṃ vidhiyogayoḥ kāryāntarbhāve 'pi atiprayojanavaśāt pṛthagabhidhānaṃ kṛtvā pañcānām eva samāsādaya uktā ity ataḥ pañcaiva padārthā ucyante ||
children.translated_text: Thus, although injunction and yoga are included within effect, because of their exceeding importance they have been stated separately, and condensations and the like have been stated only for the five; therefore only five categories are taught.
But others describe the division of the categories differently:
tattva, guṇa, and bhāva.
There, what is not dependent on anything is tattva.
And that is divided into twenty kinds.

children.text: pañca pṛthivyādīni trayodaśendriyāṇi paśuḥ kāraṇaṃ ceti ||
children.translated_text: They are the five beginning with earth, the thirteen senses, paśu, and the cause.

children.text: tattvavṛttayaḥ bhāvāśrayā guṇās tatra pṛthivyādiṣu yathāsambhavaṃ rūparasagandhasparśaśabdāḥ pañcaiva vartante ||
children.translated_text: Guṇas are functions of tattvas and have bhāva as their support; among these, in earth and the others, according to possibility, the five alone occur: form, taste, smell, touch, and sound.
But the sense-tattvas are without guṇas.
In paśus seven guṇas occur, characterized as paśutva, dharma, adharma, citta, vidyā, effort, and desire.

children.text: sukhādīnāṃ tu tadvikāratvāt tadantarbhāva eva mṛdvikāravat ||
children.translated_text: But pleasure and the others are included within these because they are modifications of them, like modifications of clay.

children.text: kāraṇe trayo guṇāḥ kāmārthitvavipratvākhyā iti dharmibhyo 'nyānanyatvenānirvacanīyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the cause there are three guṇas, called desire, arthitva, and vipratva, which are indescribable as either different or non-different from the bearers of the properties.
The dharmas of sattva-guṇas are called bhāvas.

children.text: tadvicāraś ca satkāryavicāre kṛte iti neha kriyate ||
children.translated_text: And since their examination has been made in the examination of the existent effect, it is not undertaken here.

children.text: tad evaṃ kāraṇādiniścayajñānaṃ prathamo lābha iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus the first attainment is the determinate knowledge of cause and the rest.
He states the second attainment with the word 'tapas'.
The dharma produced by injunctions such as bathing in ash is called tapas.
Its production is ascertained even from signs such as protection and the rest.

children.text: adharmataskareṇa sanmārgād apahriyamāṇaḥ sādhakaḥ purapālasthānīyena dharmeṇa rakṣyate ||
children.translated_text: The practitioner who is being carried away from the good path by the thief that is adharma is protected by dharma, which occupies the place of a city guard.
Going from one state to another state is movement.
Contentment precisely in prescribed practice is delight.
Connection with attainment is acquisition.

children.text: yadbalena vidhiyogābhiniviṣṭasya cittaṃ rambhādīnāṃ gītavādyādibhir api kṣobhayituṃ na śakyate tanmāhātmyaṃ dharmaśaktir ity arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That by whose power the mind of one absorbed in injunction and yoga cannot be disturbed even by <s>Rambhā</s> and the others with song, music, and the like: that greatness is the power of dharma. This is the meaning.
The words atigati, sāyujya, and sthiti are synonyms of finality and yoga.

children.text: yasmin sati padārthāḥ sādhakasyādhyakṣopalabdhiyogyā bhavanti sa prakāśaḥ dvividhaḥ parāparabhedāt ||
children.translated_text: When this exists, the objects become fit for direct perception by the practitioner; that is illumination. It is twofold, by the distinction between lower and higher.

children.text: tatra yena vidhiyogasādhanāni samyag vivecayati dhyeyatattve brahmaṇi ca svaṃ cittaṃ samāhitaṃ cyutaṃ ca cyavamānaṃ ca lakṣayati so 'paraḥ prakāśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There, that by which he properly discriminates the means for applying the injunction, and observes his own mind as concentrated on <s>brahman</s>, the reality to be meditated upon, or as fallen away or in the process of falling away, is the lower illumination.

children.text: yena tu sthāpanāvasare sarvatattvāni saguṇadharmāṇy ānantyena dṛṣṭvā yojyāyojyabhāvena vivecayati sa para iti ||
children.translated_text: But that by which, at the time of establishment, having seen all realities with their qualified properties in their endlessness, he discriminates them as to what is to be joined and what is not to be joined, is called the higher one.

children.text: viṣayiṇām iṣṭaviṣayeṣv ivānicchato 'pi rudre cittavṛttipravāhaḥ samīpaṃ tad evātyantotkarṣāpannaṃ devanityatvam ity etat sarvaṃ dharmajñāpakatvenoktam iti ||
children.translated_text: The flow of mental activity toward <s>Rudra</s>, even for one who does not wish it, as toward desired objects among those who have objects, proximity, and that very divine eternality attained to extreme excellence: all this has been stated as making known <s>dharma</s>.
He states the third gain.
Now, eternality, and so on.

children.text: athetyānantarye tapo'nantaraṃ yad deve bhāvābhyāsalakṣaṇaṃ nityatvaṃ tṛtīyo lābhaḥ sa ucyate ||
children.translated_text: The word 'now' has the sense of immediate succession. The eternality in relation to the god, characterized by repeated cultivation of disposition, which comes after austerity, is called the third gain.
The meaning is not, however, perpetual conjunction.

children.text: avyucchinnapravāho nityatvam atrābhipretaṃ yathā nityapravāhā gaṅgetī ||
children.translated_text: What is intended here by eternality is an uninterrupted stream, as when one says, 'the <s>Gaṅgā</s> is an eternal stream.'
He states the fourth gain: steadiness.

children.text: doṣahetujālebhyaś chinnasya mūlākhyānivṛttau cittasya rudre 'vasthānam atyantaniścalatvaṃ sthitir ucyate ||
children.translated_text: When the mind, cut off from the networks that are causes of faults, rests in <s>Rudra</s> upon the cessation of what is called the root, its absolute immovability is called steadiness.
At the same time as that, the yogin has nine characteristics, beginning with non-attachment.
There, the complete exclusion of attachment, when it is being observed, is non-attachment.
The state in which the mind abides only in the reality of <s>Rudra</s> is yoginhood.
Having a mental activity that is being brought into conformity is eternal selfhood.
Having a mind that does not come into manifestation is unbornness.
Supreme equality is friendliness.
Being separated from body and the like is oneness.
Having passed beyond every ground for anxiety is security.
Being empty of external and internal activity is inactivity.

children.text: samastacintārahitatvaṃ vītaśokatvam ity etāni lakṣaṇāny asya yogasyātyantotkṛṣṭatvapratipādanārtham uktāni ||
children.translated_text: Being free from all care is freedom from sorrow. These characteristics have been stated in order to establish the absolute excellence of this yoga.

children.text: pañcamaṃ lābham āha siddhiś ca iti ||
children.translated_text: He states the fifth gain: and siddhi.
Siddhi has been explained before.
It is also understood from inference.

children.text: nirupacaritā muktātmānaḥ paramaiśvaryopetāḥ puruṣatve sati samastaduḥkhabījarahitatvān maheśvaravat ||
children.translated_text: Liberated selves, without figurative usage, are endowed with supreme sovereignty, because, while being persons, they are free from all seeds of suffering, like <s>Maheśvara</s>.
The liberated selves accepted by others lack supreme sovereignty, because they are devoid of supreme sovereignty, like ourselves and others.
The particle 'and' indicates exclusion of deficiency and excess.
The word 'fifth' is for the sake of summing up the gains as five.

children.text: athaite lābhāḥ kiṃ deśaniyamena prāptavyā yathā brahmacārigṛhasthavānaprasthabhikṣubhir vidyāprajātayogākhyā lābhāḥ kiṃ vā deśāniyamenāpi pañcaviṃśatitattvajñena kaivalyavad iti ||
children.translated_text: Now, are these gains to be obtained only with restriction as to place, just as the gains called knowledge, progeny, and yoga are obtained by students, householders, forest-dwellers, and mendicants? Or can they also be obtained without restriction as to place, like isolation by one who knows the twenty-five realities?
The answer is given.
With restriction as to place.
For that purpose he says this.
Or, because it is from the seers, there is no fault even if it is just as heard.
