children.text: guruḥ pūrvoktas tadājñayāvatiṣṭhamānas tadāśrito bhavati yathā grāmaṇyam āśrito grāma iti ||
children.translated_text: The guru is the one mentioned before; one who remains under his command is dependent on him, as a village is dependent on its headman.

children.text: tatrādidharmāvasthasya tāvadāyatane vāsa ityatrāyatanaśabdo gurāv eva draṣṭavyo liṅgakartetyādijñāpakādupacārād vā pañcaśabdavat ||
children.translated_text: There, in the statement that one who is in the first state of dharma dwells in an āyatana, the word āyatana should be understood as referring precisely to the guru, on the evidence of such expressions as 'the maker of the liṅga,' or by figurative usage, as with the word 'five.'

children.text: yadyapyāyatanasūtre pratiṣedhaḥ śrūyate tathāpi deśaprastāve gururabhipreta evācāryo loka ityādi jñāpakābhyanujñānāt ||
children.translated_text: Although a prohibition is heard in the āyatana-sūtra, nevertheless in the context of place the guru alone is intended, because of indications and permissions such as 'the teacher is the world.'

children.text: ata eva gūḍhavratopadeśādāyatane vāsa ityatrāyatanaśabdo jane vivakṣito maryādayāyatanāditi kṛtvā baddhasya rudrasya hi śivāyatanavāsānupapatteḥ ||
children.translated_text: For this very reason, because of the instruction on the hidden vow, in the statement 'dwelling in an āyatana' the word āyatana is intended to mean people, since they are the boundary and support; for a bound <s>Rudra</s> dwelling in the abode of <s>Śiva</s> is not possible.

children.text: yadāpi vāsastadāpi janādhīna evetyato dvitīyāvasthasya jana eva deśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Even when there is dwelling, it depends on people; therefore for one in the second state, people alone are the place.
By the word 'people' here are denoted those belonging to the classes and life-stages who are qualified for the production of dharma and adharma.
For one in the third state, a cave is the place.

children.text: guhāgrahaṇaṃ sūtrārthopalakṣaṇārtham ataḥ śūnyāgāraguhayoranyataraṃ vyāsaṅgādidoṣavarjitaṃ yatprāpyate tatra vastavyam ||
children.translated_text: The mention of a cave is meant to indicate the meaning of the sūtra. Therefore, whichever of an empty house or a cave, free from faults such as attachment, is obtained, one should dwell there.

children.text: deśagrahaṇaṃ tatrāvasthānamātreṇa guhāyā deśatvajñāpanārthaṃ na tu gurujanavat tadāyattatveneti ||
children.translated_text: The mention of place is for making known that the cave is a place merely by residence there, not because of dependence on it as in the case of the guru and people.
For one in the fourth state, the place is a cremation ground.
And the cremation ground should be taken in its well-known sense.

children.text: tasya ca na guhāvaddeśatvaṃ kiṃ tv ā dehapātāt tatraivānirgacchatā stheyam ityayaṃ viśeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Its being a place is not like that of a cave; rather, the distinction is this: one should remain right there, without leaving, until the fall of the body.
For one in the fifth state, the place is <s>Rudra</s>.
<s>Rudra</s> is the blessed <s>Maheśvara</s>.

children.text: prāgapi rudrāyattatvāt sādhakasya rudro'styeva deśastathāpi prāganyavyapadeśo 'pyasti sāmprataṃ punaḥ śarīrādirahitasya sarvadeśavikalatvād avadhāraṇaṃ karoti rudra eveti ||
children.translated_text: Even before this, because the practitioner is dependent on <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Rudra</s> is indeed his place; nevertheless, previously there was also another designation. But now, since one who is without body and the like lacks all other places, he makes the restriction: <s>Rudra</s> alone.
The particle 'and' excludes deficiency and excess.
Now, are these gains obtained merely by abiding in that place, as one who stands in the place of a wish-fulfilling tree obtains things?
The answer is given.
No.
What then? Just as there is a difference of places, there is also a difference of means.
For the purpose of setting that forth, he says:

children.text: grahaṇadhāraṇohāpohavijñānavacanakriyāyathānyāyābhiniveśānāṃ vāsa iti saṃjñā tāntrikī śiṣṭaiḥ kṛtā ||
children.translated_text: The technical designation vāsa has been made by learned authorities for grasping, retaining, inference, exclusion, understanding, speech, action, and attachment according to the proper method.
Among these, grasping is the capacity for correct apprehension of the meaning of a sentence uttered once.
Retention is the capacity to remember what has been grasped even after a long interval of time.
Inference is the capacity to apprehend an unprecedented meaning from hearing one part, by applying its principle.
Exclusion is the capacity to accept or reject meanings stated by those who resemble teachers, through the discrimination of what is reasonable and unreasonable.
Understanding is the capacity for examining a heard meaning in many ways and for explaining it to another.
Speech is a sentence free from faults such as contradiction and repetition.
For one who pleases the teacher by faultless pronunciation of words, vidyā becomes manifest when the impurity of false cognition has ceased.
Likewise service to the guru, such as rising and going forward to meet him, is called action.

When the meaning of scripture, not contradicting what precedes and follows, is examined even by reasoning, the intense effort to put that meaning into practice is attachment according to the proper method.
And so it has been said:
He who, by reasoning, investigates the unshaken meaning of a sentence
without contradiction between what precedes and what follows, knows <s>dharma</s>; no one else does.
Conduct is the means to <s>dharma</s>.
The group of actions beginning with ash-bathing and ending in mūḍha is called conduct.
And it has three limbs: the limbs of giving, sacrifice, and austerity.
When the five purifying formulas are being repeated, the dedication of oneself to <s>Parameśvara</s> with ten obeisances is giving.
That very same is supreme giving, because its fruit is non-return.
The other, however, is bad giving, because its fruit is return.
Sacrifice is the performance, as prescribed, of actions such as ash-bathing, with the intention of fulfilling <s>Parameśvara</s>'s command.
That very same is supreme sacrifice; the other is bad sacrifice, for the two reasons stated before.

children.text: svavidhyabhiniviṣṭasyaiva trividhaduḥkhopanipāte sati anupāyataḥ pratīkāramakurvataḥ sahiṣṇutvaṃ tāpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Austerity is the endurance of one who is intent on his own rule, when the threefold suffering befalls him, and who does not seek a remedy because there is no means.
That very same is supreme austerity; the other is bad austerity.

children.text: sā tryaṅgāpi caryā dvividhā vrataṃ dvārāṇi ceti ||
children.translated_text: That conduct, though three-limbed, is also twofold: vow and gateways.

children.text: tatra snānaśayanopahārajapapradakṣiṇāni vratam dharmaniṣpattyadharmocchedārthaṃ prādhānyena kriyamāṇatvāt ||
children.translated_text: Among these, bathing, lying down, offering, recitation, and circumambulation are the vow, because they are performed principally for the production of <s>dharma</s> and the cutting off of adharma.
The gateways, however, are snoring, trembling, limping, amorous display, acting as if wounded, and speaking accordingly.

children.text: apamānaparibhavaparivādaniṣpādanadvāreṇa pūrvotpannayor dharmādharmayor āyavyayanimittatvāditi kramaḥ svarūpaṃ caiṣāṃ bhāṣya eva prapañcitam ||
children.translated_text: This is the sequence, because through the gateway of producing contempt, insult, and blame, they become causes for the acquisition and expenditure of the previously arisen <s>dharma</s> and adharma; their nature has been elaborated in the commentary itself.
Following that, I too will show it briefly for the benefit of disciples.
Two ghaṭikās before sunrise is the morning twilight.
It has three deities.

children.text: prathamā brāhmī madhyamā vaiṣṇavī antyā raudrī ||
children.translated_text: The first is Brāhmī, the middle is Vaiṣṇavī, and the last is Raudrī.

children.text: tatra pūrvasaṃdhyayoḥ śaucaṃ kṛtvā bhasma saṃskartavyam ||
children.translated_text: At the earlier twilights, having performed purification, the ash should be consecrated.

children.text: kartṛkārakādidoṣarahitaṃ śuklādiguṇayuktaṃ ca bhasmārjitaṃ śivadakṣiṇamūrtau mantraiḥ saṃskṛtya pradakṣiṇaṃ ca dattvā sūryarūpiṇaṃ bhagavantaṃ locanatrayeṇa prasannadṛṣṭyā bhasma paśyantaṃ dhyāyet ||
children.translated_text: Having obtained ash free from faults of agency, instrument, and the like, and endowed with qualities such as whiteness, one should consecrate it with mantras at the southern form of <s>Śiva</s>, perform circumambulation, and meditate on the blessed one in the form of the sun, who with his three eyes looks upon the ash with gracious sight.

children.text: tadanu cācāryāya śivatattvānurañjitadṛṣṭaye jyeṣṭhabhrātre vā nivedayet ||
children.translated_text: After that one should present it to the teacher, whose sight is colored by the reality of <s>Śiva</s>, or to an elder brother.

children.text: tadanv ekānte śucau pradeśe jantusthāvarahīne pañca pavitrāṇyāvartayataiva stheyaṃ raudrasavanaṃ yāvattato bhagavantaṃ praṇamya tvadājñāṃ karomītyabhisaṃdhāya japannaivāpādatalamastakaṃ yāvat prabhūtena bhasmanāṅgaṃ pratyaṅgaṃ ca prayatnātiśayena nighṛṣya nighṛṣya snānamācared ityevaṃ madhyāhnāparāhṇasaṃdhyayor apīti ||
children.translated_text: Then, in a solitary, pure place free from moving and stationary creatures, one should remain while repeating the five purifying formulas until the Raudra period; then, having bowed to the blessed one and resolved, 'I carry out your command,' while reciting, from the soles of the feet up to the head, one should repeatedly rub each limb and subsidiary limb with abundant ash with exceptional care, and perform the bath. It is the same at the midday and afternoon twilights as well.
Only this much is distinctive here.

children.text: madhyāhne prathamā brāhmī madhye mastakoparisthite ravau raudrī tadante vaiṣṇavī arkāstasamayottaratra prathamā raudrī tadanu vaiṣṇavī tadante brāhmī ceti ||
children.translated_text: At midday, the first is Brāhmī; when the sun is in the middle, above the head, it is Raudrī; at its end it is Vaiṣṇavī. After the time of sunset, the first is Raudrī, then Vaiṣṇavī, and at the end Brāhmī.
Everywhere the Raudra period alone is the time for bathing.

children.text: evaṃ snānaṃ nirvartya japann evāyatanaṃ gatvā śivaṃ bhaktyatiśayena praṇamya snānaṃ nivedya ca śanairgarbhagṛhaṃ praviśet ||
children.translated_text: Having completed the bath in this way, while still reciting, one should go to the shrine, bow to <s>Śiva</s> with intense devotion, report the bath, and slowly enter the inner sanctum.

children.text: tadanu mūrtidakṣiṇe deśe jānunī pātayitvā hṛdi cāñjaliṃ baddhvā mūrtisthaṃ sākṣādiva śivaṃ paśyan yadyanivṛttapratyāhārastadā gatamātra eva hasitaṃ kuryādityeke ||
children.translated_text: After that, in the place to the south of the image, having placed both knees on the ground, joined the hands at the heart, and looked upon <s>Śiva</s> situated in the image as if directly present, if one has not yet completed withdrawal, then immediately upon arrival one should perform laughter, according to some.

children.text: vayaṃ tu paśyāmo'bhigamya ca yatpūrvaṃ japatītyādi bhāṣyasyārtho yadi vicāryate tadāvaśyaṃ gatvā saṃyatātmanottarābhimukhena pratyāhāraviśeṣārthaṃ japtavyaṃ japtvā tu śivadhyānāsakta evāṭṭahāsaṃ punaḥ punaḥ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: But we think that, if the meaning of the commentary passage beginning 'having approached, what he first recites' is considered, then after going there one must necessarily recite, self-controlled and facing north, for the sake of the special withdrawal; but after reciting, while absorbed in meditation on <s>Śiva</s>, one should again and again perform loud laughter.
After that, having begun the song, one should rise while singing.
Then one should perform the dance together with the song.
There, having first completed the song, one should afterwards complete the dance.

children.text: tadanu pūrvoktavidhinopaviśya śivaṃ dhyāyanneva huḍukkāraṃ kṛtvā namaskāraṃ kuryāttadanu japamiti ||
children.translated_text: After that, having sat down according to the procedure stated before, while meditating on <s>Śiva</s> himself, he should make the huḍukkāra sound and perform obeisance; after that, japa.

children.text: atra japanamaskārau mānasāv eva nṛtyaṃ kāyikameva hasitagītahuḍukkārā vācikā eveti niyama iṣṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here the intended rule is that japa and obeisance are purely mental, dancing is purely bodily, and laughter, song, and huḍukkāra are purely vocal.

children.text: tatra dīrghocchvāsatrayaṃ yāvaddhasitaṃ daṇḍakatrirāvartanaṃ yāvadgītanṛtye gambhīrahuḍukkāratrayaṃ ṣaṣṭi namaskārān pañcapavitrāṇāṃ trir āvartanaṃ kuryādityāha bhagavānācāryaḥ svāmī mama yenāhamajñānārṇavāduttāritaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There, laughter should last for three long exhalations; song and dance should last for three repetitions of the daṇḍaka; three deep huḍukkāras should be made; sixty obeisances and three repetitions of the five purificatory formulas should be performed. So says the blessed teacher, my master, by whom I was lifted out of the ocean of ignorance.

children.text: ṭīkākārāstu sarvam ā paritoṣāt kartavyamityevaṃ pratipannāḥ ||
children.translated_text: But the commentators have understood it in this way: everything is to be done until satisfaction.

children.text: tadevaṃ nirvartyopahāraṃ dhyāyannīśaṃ hasitagītanṛtyahuḍukkāranamaskārajapyaiḥ ṣaḍaṅgopahāraṃ bhagavanmahādeva yuṣmadanujñayā nirvartitavān aham avabhṛthasnānaṃ ca kariṣyāmītyevaṃ nivedayet ||
children.translated_text: Having thus completed the offering, while meditating on <s>Īśa</s>, he should report: 'O blessed <s>Mahādeva</s>, by your permission I have completed the six-limbed offering with laughter, song, dance, huḍukkāra, obeisance, and japa, and I shall perform the avabhṛtha bath.'

children.text: tato niṣkramyeśaṃ praṇamya praṇāmāntaṃ pradakṣiṇatrayaṃ japann eva śanaiḥ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: Then, having gone out and bowed to <s>Īśa</s>, he should slowly perform three circumambulations ending with prostration, while continuing japa.

children.text: tato'vabhṛthasnānaṃ kṛtvā bhagavaṃllakulīśādīn rāśīkarāntāṃśca tīrthakarānanukrameṇa yathāvadbhaktyā namaskuryāt tadanu pradakṣiṇamekamiti ||
children.translated_text: Then, after performing the avabhṛtha bath, he should bow in sequence and with proper devotion to the blessed <s>Lakulīśa</s> and the others, the tīrthakaras down to <s>Rāśīkara</s>; after that, one circumambulation.

children.text: anyadā tu yāvadicchaṃ pradakṣiṇaṃ japann eva kuryāt pañcamantrajapastu kevalo'pi dharmahetur iti ||
children.translated_text: At other times, however, he should perform circumambulation as much as he wishes, while continuing japa; and recitation of the five mantras, even by itself, is a cause of dharma.

children.text: athāyatanasaṃdhinaṃ deśaṃ divā parigṛhītasthāvarādidoṣavarjitatvena suparīkṣitaṃ saṃdhyāvasāne vastrāntādimṛdupavitreṇa vivecya bhasmanaiva śuciṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: Next, during the day he should choose a place adjoining the shrine, well examined as free from the defects of immovable objects and the like that have been occupied; at the end of twilight he should inspect it with a soft purifier such as the edge of a garment and make it clean with ash alone.

children.text: tadanu tatropaviśya vidhyabhiniviṣṭas tāvat tiṣṭhed yāvad atinidrābhibhūtaḥ śrāntaśca bhavati ||
children.translated_text: After that, having sat there and being intent on the injunction, he should remain as long as it takes for him to become overcome by excessive sleep and tired.
Then he should rise again and inspect it.

children.text: tadanu mantraiḥ saṃskṛtya bhasma prabhūtaṃ prastaret ||
children.translated_text: After that, having consecrated it with mantras, he should spread abundant ash.

children.text: tatastatra pañca mantrānāvartayanneva svapet punarutthāyānenaiva vidhinā svapedyenāśveva śuddhivṛddhī bhavataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then he should sleep there while repeating the five mantras. Having risen again, he should sleep by this very procedure, whereby purification and increase occur overnight.

children.text: suptasyāpi prāṇātyaye cātigatiḥ syādanyathā vidhibhraṣṭasya saṃsārāpattir eveti ||
children.translated_text: Even for one who is asleep, if life should end, there would be an excellent destiny; otherwise, for one who has fallen from the rule, there is only falling into saṃsāra.

children.text: evaṃ prathamāvasthāyāṃ vidhim anuṣṭhāya yadā khalu prāptajñānaḥ prakṣīṇakaluṣaḥ kṛtābhyanujñaśca bhavati tadāvasthāntaraṃ gatvā raṅgavadavasthiteṣu janeṣu madhye naṭavadavasthito vivecya vivecya krāthanādīni kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: Having thus practiced the rule in the first stage, when he has attained knowledge, his impurity has been exhausted, and he has received permission, then, having entered another stage, he should stand like an actor in the midst of people who are standing as though in a theater, and after careful discrimination perform krāthana and the other acts.

children.text: tatrāsuptasyeva suptaliṅgapradarśanaṃ krāthanaṃ vāyvabhibhūtasyeva śarīrāvayavānāṃ kampanaṃ spandanam upahatapādendriyasyeva gamanaṃ mandanam ||
children.translated_text: Among these, displaying the sign of being asleep while not asleep is krāthana; shaking the limbs of the body as though overcome by wind is spandana; going about as though the faculty of the feet were impaired is mandana.

children.text: yauvanasampannāṃ striyamavalokayan kāmukam ivātmānaṃ yair liṅgaiḥ pradarśayati tac chṛṅgāraṇaṃ kāryākāryavivekaśūnyasyeva lokaninditakaraṇam api tatkaraṇaṃ vyāhatāpārthakādiśabdoccāraṇam api tad bhāṣaṇam iti ||
children.translated_text: When, looking at a woman endowed with youth, he displays himself by signs as though he were lustful, that is śṛṅgāraṇa; doing what is censured by people as though he lacked discrimination between what should and should not be done is tatkaraṇa; and uttering contradictory, meaningless, and similar words is tadbhāṣaṇa.
And no fixed sequence is prescribed for these.

children.text: kiṃtvapamānādiniṣpādakatvaṃ yena paribhavaṃ gacched ityupadeśād davāgnitulyatvenāpamānāder iṣṭatamatvād iti ||
children.translated_text: Rather, because the instruction is 'by that by which he would undergo humiliation,' their function is to produce contempt and the like; for contempt and the like are most desired because they are like a forest fire.
If so, then there would also be the occasion for committing violence, theft, and so forth, and for uttering corrupt words, since these too produce contempt and the like.

No, because the undertaking of krāthana and the rest is for the purpose of making known, within the full scope of divine actions, that there is no contradiction with non-violence and the other restraints, even though one does those acts and speaks in that way.

children.text: devanityatve kastarhi upāya ityāha japadhyānam iti ||
children.translated_text: If the deity is eternal, then what is the means? He answers: japa and meditation.
There, japa is the repetition of the third and fourth mantras.
It is twofold: that whose result is pratyāhāra and that whose result is samādhi.

children.text: tatrādyaḥ pratyāhāraphalastanniṣpattau ca kriyamāṇo japaḥ samādhiphala iti ||
children.translated_text: There, the first is whose result is pratyāhāra; and when japa is performed after that has been accomplished, it has samādhi as its result.

children.text: nanu cānyāsaktatve kriyamāṇo japaḥ saṃvatsaraśatenāpi na pratyāhāraṃ karotyapi tu doṣameva tasya janayatīti ||
children.translated_text: But, one might object, japa performed while one is attached to other things does not bring about pratyāhāra even in a hundred years; rather, it produces only fault for that person.
That is exactly true.
But here pratyāhāra is accepted as twofold, divided into higher and lower.
There, the lower is preceded by the internal organ.

children.text: tatsahitena japena nirmalīkṛtaṃ cittaṃ prayatnanirapekṣamapi brahmaṇyevālātacakravad avatiṣṭhate yadā tadāsau paraḥ pratyāhāro japapūrvaka evāyam ityuktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the mind, purified by japa together with that, remains in <s>Brahman</s> alone like a whirling firebrand, even without depending on effort, then that is the higher pratyāhāra; this too is said to be preceded by japa.

children.text: sa hy anekajanmopārjitaṃ karma lakṣaṇamātreṇa dagdhvā dhyeyatattve cittaṃ stambhanikṣiptāyaḥkīlakavan niścalīkaroti ||
children.translated_text: For, by merely characterizing it, it burns up karma accumulated over many births and makes the mind motionless in the meditated principle, like an iron peg driven into a post.
Meditation is a continuous flow of thought similar to the <s>Rudra</s> principle.
That is twofold: preceded by japa and preceded by dhāraṇā.

children.text: tatra japapūrvakaṃ prasaṅgenaiva pūrvam uktaṃ dhāraṇāpūrvakaṃ tūcyate ||
children.translated_text: There, what is preceded by japa has already been stated incidentally; now what is preceded by dhāraṇā is stated.
For one who is not deluded, dhāraṇā is the mind without an object-support.

children.text: saṃhṛtamūrchādyavasthasyāpi cittaṃ vṛttālābhānnirālambanam astīti tannivṛttyartham amūḍhasyetyuktam ||
children.translated_text: Since even the mind of one in a state of restrained stupor and the like is without an object-support because it does not obtain a mental modification, the phrase 'of one who is not deluded' is stated in order to exclude that.

children.text: yo vidyānugṛhītayā buddhyā svaṃ cittaṃ nirālambanaṃ karoti so 'mūḍha ityucyate ||
children.translated_text: He who, with an intellect favored by knowledge, makes his own mind without any object-support is called 'not deluded.'

children.text: tayā dhāraṇayā nirmalīkṛtaṃ cittaṃ rudratattve sthāpitaṃ sudīrghakālaṃ na cyavata ityanenaiva viśeṣeṇa pūrvadhyānāpekṣayedaṃ dhāraṇāsahitaṃ dhyānaṃ paramityuktaṃ śrīmadbhāṣyakṛtā paramayoginā ||
children.translated_text: The mind purified by that <s>dhāraṇā</s> (fixation), established in the <s>Rudra</s> principle, does not fall away for a very long time. By precisely this distinction, this meditation accompanied by <s>dhāraṇā</s> is called supreme, in comparison with the preceding meditation, by the venerable author of the commentary, the supreme yogin.

children.text: yadyapyeva dīkṣāprabhṛti cittaṃ nirmalīkartuṃ na śakyate tathāpi dhānuṣkacitrakarādivad abhyāsārthaṃ sarvāvasthāsu yathāśaktyā dhyānaṃ kartavyaṃ mṛtyukālasyāniścitatvāt ||
children.translated_text: Although the mind cannot be purified in this way from initiation onward, nevertheless, like an archer, painter, and so on, one should practice meditation in every condition according to one's ability, because the time of death is uncertain.

children.text: anyathā hi yuddhakāla eva aśvadamananyāyaḥ syāditi ||
children.translated_text: Otherwise it would be like the maxim of taming a horse only at the time of battle.

children.text: itthaṃ samyagvidhiṃ jñātvā yastu dhyāyati śaṃkaram
children.translated_text: Thus, one who has correctly understood the rule and meditates on <s>Śaṃkara</s>,
at the beginning of night, at midnight, and at night's end, without falling from his vow,

children.text: yāmaṃ yāmaṃ tadarghaṃ yāvacchaktyā divāpi ca
children.translated_text: for a watch, a watch, or half of that, and also by day according to his ability,
abandoning attachment elsewhere and seeing worldly existence as full of suffering,
taking up supreme detachment, eating lightly, and having conquered his senses,
exerting extraordinary effort and increasing the excellence of purity,
continuously for six months, even if he is guilty of brahmin-murder and the like,
or for one full year, would become one whose mind is fixed on that and who is made of that.

children.text: sa hatvā duṣkṛtaṃ ghoraṃ rāgādīnāṃ ca pañjaram
children.translated_text: Having destroyed dreadful evil and the cage of passion and the rest,
he directly sees the whole principle, furnished with all limiting adjuncts.
Seeing the lord of all beings, the infinite, imperishable <s>Śiva</s>,
who is not seen even by lords of yoga other than the Pāśupatas,

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā paramaiśvaryaṃ labdhvā syānnirbhayaḥ sadā
children.translated_text: and having seen him and obtained supreme sovereignty, he would always be fearless.
Even if, not knowing the procedure, a man of good vows
always meditates on <s>Śaṃkara</s> at those times with true devotion, zeal, and detachment,
for him too the pleased Lord would grant that unsurpassed siddhi.
Having attained it, he has abandoned saṃsāra and, independent, becomes like <s>Śiva</s>.
If, while meditating on that <s>Īśāna</s> alone, he gives up his breaths,

children.text: tasya dehāntakāle vai dadyādīśaḥ parāṃ gatim
children.translated_text: then at the time of the end of his body the Lord would indeed grant him the supreme destination.
Those who live on water, those who live on air, and those who practice extremely fierce austerities,
and those who give earth and the like and perform sacrifices,
the siddhi which they obtain in a thousand years,
a yati devoted to japa and meditation obtains in half a watch.
Knowing in this way the greatness of yoga and the uncertainty of the body's continuance and the like,

children.text: duḥkhārṇavaṃ ca saṃsāraṃ na kuryādanyathā matim
children.translated_text: and that saṃsāra is an ocean of suffering, he should not direct his mind otherwise.
As long as the body is maintained and as long as the intellect does not decline,
so long should he practice meditation and japa according to his ability.
Just as someone thinks day and night of a desired possession that has been lost,
so, without laziness, he should meditate on <s>Śiva</s>, untouched by speech and the other faculties.
Just as, for one who wishes to speak, a word first shines in the mind, purified from speech,

children.text: tadvattaṃ praṇidhānena divā rātrau ca cintayet ||
children.translated_text: so should he contemplate him with concentration by day and at night.
Or, having conceived him as distinguished by qualities and attributes, and quickly become certain,
afterwards he should meditate on him alone, having separated him from those by the intellect.

children.text: ityetat pāśupatayogavidhānaṃ paramottamaṃ surairapi alabhyaṃ paramaguhyam ā parameśvarād gurupāramparyopadeśaikasamadhigamyaṃ svalpaprajñānām anugrahārthaṃ vyaktam evopanyastam ||
children.translated_text: Thus this supreme and highest rule of Pāśupata yoga, unattainable even by the gods, most secret, and knowable only through the instruction of a lineage of teachers beginning with <s>Parameśvara</s>, has been set forth plainly for the sake of favoring those of slight understanding.

children.text: yastvevaṃ na śraddadhātyaparīkṣitebhyo vā dadāti tasya brahmahatyādibhyo 'pi garīyaḥ pātakaṃ syād ityataḥ śiṣyaparīkṣāyāṃ śraddhāyāṃ ca yatnaḥ kartavya iti ||
children.translated_text: But one who does not have faith in this, or gives it to those who have not been examined, would incur a sin heavier even than brahmin-murder and the like. Therefore effort must be made regarding the examination of the disciple and regarding faith.
He states the means to stability.
'And likewise constant remembrance of <s>Rudra</s>.'
The very eternality of the deity is called constant remembrance.
The use of another technical term is for the purpose of teaching that it is a means with respect to stability.
The word 'likewise' has the sense of similarity.

children.text: yathā devanityatvaṃ pratyadhyayanadhyānayorevopāyatvaṃ dharmaṃ ca prati caryāyā eva tadanugrāhakatvenānusnānādiyamayantraṇādir apyupāyatvam upacaryate tathā sthitiṃ prati smṛtireva prādhānyenopāyas tadanugrāhakatvenendriyajayo 'pyupāyatvenokta ityato nendriyajayād ityanena virodhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Just as, with respect to the eternality of the deity, study and meditation alone are the means, and with respect to <s>dharma</s> only conduct is the means, while bathing afterwards and similar restraints are figuratively called means because they assist it, so with respect to stability remembrance alone is principally the means, while conquest of the senses is also stated as a means because it assists that. Therefore there is no contradiction with the statement 'from conquest of the senses.'
Some say that conquest of the senses is another means for the cessation of attachment and the like.
That is not so, because it conflicts with there being five means and because it conflicts with the commentary on the sūtra concerning abandonment and taking up.
Others also say that eternality of the deity and conquest of the senses are identical.
That too is not so.
Because their definitions differ: mastery over releasing and restraining the senses is conquest of the senses.
Devotion to the repeated cultivation of the deity is the eternality of the deity.
Then, since the means to siddhi must be stated, he says:
'And grace alone.'
The cause's wish to give its own qualities is called <s>prasāda</s> (grace).
The word 'and' indicates the exclusion of deficiency and excess.
The word 'alone' determines that grace does not depend on anything else.

children.text: lābhānāmupāyā ityetad gamyamānārthasyāpyabhidhānaṃ śāstrāntaroktānāṃ mokṣopāyānām anupāyatvajñāpanārtham ||
children.translated_text: The phrase 'the means to the attainments,' though its meaning is already understood, is stated in order to make known that the means to liberation taught in other śāstras are not means here.
The word 'five' is for summing up.
'Established' means 'seen by trustworthy authorities.'

children.text: atha kimetairupāyaiḥ pañcalābhā eva prāptavyā iti na kiṃ tarhi malāśca pañca kṣapaṇīyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now, is it the case that by these means only the five gains are to be attained? No. Rather, the five impurities also are to be destroyed.
Which are they? He states this.

children.text: tatra pramāṇābhāsajaṃ jñānaṃ mithyājñānam uktaṃ saṃśayaviparyayādilakṣaṇam ||
children.translated_text: There, the cognition produced by a pseudo-means of knowledge is false knowledge, already described as having the character of doubt, error, and the like.

children.text: śāstrāntarebhyo'pi tarhi saṃśayādinivṛtter aviśeṣaprasaṅga iti cen na śāstrāntarapraṇetṝṇām api viparyayānivṛttipratipādanād ācāryavaiśeṣyaprakaraṇe ||
children.translated_text: If it is objected that then the cessation of doubt and the like would follow without distinction even from other scriptures, the answer is no, because in the section on the teacher's distinctiveness it is taught that even the authors of other scriptures have not removed error.
Therefore the cessation of doubt and the like does not come even from other scriptures.
Desire, anger, and hatred are defilement; that too is included under ignorance.
Why?
Because, when it reaches the unmanifest state, it stands as an antagonist.

children.text: tadidaṃ saṃśayādi kaluṣaṃ ca saha bījena mithyājñānam ityucyate ||
children.translated_text: Thus this doubt and the like, together with defilement and with its seed, is called false knowledge.
He shows the second impurity with the words, 'and adharma.'
Here 'adharma' is intended to mean the seed of sin, sin itself.
Its being one impurity together with its transformations is because what transforms and its transformation are not different.

children.text: saty apy ajñānakaluṣasaṅgacyutihetor adharmatve pāpākhya evātrādharmo 'bhipreta iti caḥ sūcayati ||
children.translated_text: Although adharma is also the cause of the falling away of the conjunction of ignorance and defilement, the word 'and' indicates that here the adharma intended is specifically what is called sin.
He states the third impurity.
'The cause of attachment.'

children.text: saktiḥ saṅgaḥ viṣayāsaktilakṣaṇasukhaṃ bhāṣye sukhābhimāna ityanenoktam ||
children.translated_text: Attachment is clinging. The pleasure characterized by attachment to objects is what is called in the commentary 'the conceit of pleasure.'

children.text: tasyaiva lakṣaṇārthaṃ bhāṣyam avivecanamiśraṇapreraṇalakṣaṇo vanagajavat iti ||
children.translated_text: For the purpose of defining that very thing, the commentary says: 'It has the character of non-discrimination, mixture, and instigation, like a forest elephant.'

children.text: tasya saṅgasya hetus tanmayakaraṇaṃ vidhyantaropārjito dharmaḥ saṅgakara iti ya uktaḥ saha vikāreṇāsau tṛtīyo mala iti ||
children.translated_text: The cause of that attachment is dharma acquired through another prescribed rite, making one absorbed in that; the dharma that was called 'producer of attachment,' together with its transformation, is the third impurity.
He states the fourth impurity.
'And lapse likewise.'

children.text: rudratattvādīṣaccittaṃ cyavate viṣayaṃ na prāpnoti taccittacyavanaṃ cyutir ityucyate ||
children.translated_text: The mind slips a little from the <s>Rudra</s> principle and the like and does not reach the object; that slipping of the mind is called lapse.
The word 'likewise' has the sense of similarity.

children.text: yathā mithyājñānasya svabījena saha malatvam adharmasaṅgakarayoś ca savikāreṇa tathā cyuterapi ūṣmavad avasthitādharmākhyena svabījena saha malatvam iti ||
children.translated_text: Just as false knowledge is an impurity together with its own seed, and adharma and the producer of attachment are impurities together with their transformations, so lapse too is an impurity together with its own seed called adharma, which remains like heat.

children.text: atra bhāṣyavirodhānna mithyājñānakaluṣapāpmasaṅgacyutayaḥ puruṣasya bhāvāś cittavidyayor vā ||
children.translated_text: Here, because of conflict with the commentary, false knowledge, defilement, sin, attachment, and lapse are not states of the person, nor of consciousness and knowledge.

children.text: nāpi kaluṣamicchāyā bhāvaḥ kiṃtvadharmavikārā evaite jñānecchābhyāṃ saha kṣīrodakavad abhinnā iva gṛhyante ||
children.translated_text: Nor is defilement a state of desire. Rather, these are transformations of adharma alone, and they are apprehended together with knowledge and desire as if undivided, like milk and water.
And this has been elaborated in the discussion of the existent effect.
He states the fifth impurity: 'paśutva.'
<s>Paśutva</s>, being a bound soul, is a quality of the person distinct from dharma and adharma and inferred from obstruction.
It is an impurity furnished with fourteen characteristics.

children.text: tāni ca lakṣaṇāny asarvajñatvādīny apatitvāntāni sarvajñatvādiviparyayeṇaiva vyākhyātānīti ||
children.translated_text: And those characteristics, beginning with non-omniscience and ending with being unfallen, have been explained precisely as the opposites of omniscience and the rest.

children.text: taccetthaṃbhūtaṃ paśutvaṃ saṃsārasyānādikāraṇaṃ pradhānabhūtam ityevaṃ matvāha mūlamiti ||
children.translated_text: Considering that <s>paśutva</s> of this sort is the beginningless principal cause of saṃsāra, he says 'root.'
For even those who have gone to isolation, though the other impurities are absent, fall again into saṃsāra because of <s>paśutva</s> alone.
The word 'five' is for summing up by excluding both fewer and more.
'These' is for emphasis.

children.text: ete eva saṃsārabandhātmakā malā na tu śāstrāntaroktā bhoktṛbhogyasambandhādaya ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The meaning is: these alone are the impurities consisting in bondage to saṃsāra, not the relations of enjoyer and enjoyed and so on taught in other scriptures.
Where, then, are impurities of this sort well known? He answers.

children.text: tantre sākṣān maheśvarapraṇītam athaśabdādi śivāntaṃ śāstraṃ tantraṃ tasminnete pratipāditā ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the tantra: the scripture directly taught by <s>Maheśvara</s>, beginning with the word 'atha' and ending with <s>Śiva</s>, is the tantra; in that, these are taught. This is the meaning.

children.text: dharmajñānāderapi tyajyamānatvād adharmāderiva malatvaṃ prāptamityāśaṅkyāha heyādhikārataḥ iti ||
children.translated_text: Since dharma, knowledge, and the like are also abandoned, one might suppose that they too, like adharma and the rest, are impurities. To address this he says: 'because of the authority concerning what is to be rejected.'

children.text: yeṣāṃ kardamādivadduḥkhahetutvaṃ matvā sādhakaḥ kṣapaṇārtham adhikriyate ta eva malā na tu yeṣāṃ puṣpādivadanicchato'pi vināśa ityato heyādhikārād ajñānādaya eva malā iti ||
children.translated_text: Those things alone are impurities whose being causes of suffering, like mud and the like, is recognized, and for whose destruction the practitioner is authorized; not those whose destruction occurs even when one does not desire it, like flowers and the like. Therefore, because of the authority concerning what is to be rejected, ignorance and the rest alone are impurities.
Or the reading may be 'having authority as rejectable'; there too this is the meaning.

children.text: heyatvena kṣapaṇīyatvenādhikāro yogyatāsti yeṣāṃ te heyādhikāriṇasta eva heyādhikārikāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those for which there is authorization, that is fitness, as things to be rejected and destroyed are 'authorized as rejectable'; those very things are 'having rejectability-authority.'
The suffix -ka is used in its own sense.

children.text: adhikāraśabdād vā ikaṅpratyaye kṛte heyapadena karmadhārayas tadayamartho yato heyādhikārikā evātra malā vivakṣitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Or, when the suffix -ika is added to the word 'authority,' there is a karmadhāraya compound with the word 'rejectable.' Thus the meaning is that only those things authorized as rejectable are intended here as impurities.
Therefore dharma, knowledge, dispassion, and the like are not impurities too.
All this, ocean-like, has been declared by me in summary:
through the grace of the teachers, the knowledge characterized by the five categories.
What use is the knowing of many scriptures, which steal away one's own practice?
Having known this alone as supreme, one should become devoted to the practice of yoga.
But the person who, after hearing this, considers himself one whose task is accomplished:
to him this knowledge should be given by one who desires success, not to another.
But whoever, for any reason, should give it to those who lack the proper bounds,
because of breaking the secret, he goes with his pupils to a downward destiny.
Reverence to that true guru, who has reached the end of all knowledge,
by whom the ocean of the five categories has been displayed in eight good verses.
